(2) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both.
ingredients: Party to a criminal conspiracy
(1) Conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment of two years or upwards
(2) Any other criminal conspiracy

punishment_options.type: Same punishment as for abetment of the offence
punishment_options.condition: (1) Conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, life imprisonment or RI of two years or more
(2) Up to six months — other conspiracies

sections.key_principle: Two-tier: conspiracy to commit serious offences is punished as abetment (so it can attract the punishment of the offence itself); other conspiracies — up to six months. Commonly charged together with the substantive offence.

subsections.text: Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence.

Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences Against the State

chapters_covered: VI — Of Offences Against the State
key_themes: Waging war against the Government of India, attempt and abetment (s. 121); conspiracy (s. 121A); preparation (s. 122); concealment of design (s. 123)
Assault on the President/Governor to coerce lawful powers (s. 124)
Sedition (s. 124A) — constitutional status and Supreme Court order of 2022
Offences relating to allied Asiatic Powers — war, depredation, receiving property (ss. 125–127)
State prisoners and prisoners of war — public servant's voluntary/negligent escape and third-party aid (ss. 128–130)
notable_amendments: Act 16 of 1921 — forfeiture of all property replaced by fine in ss. 121, 122; s. 121A fine added.
Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 — 'transportation for life' replaced by 'imprisonment for life' in ss. 121A, 122, 124A, 125, 128, 130.
Act 27 of 1870 — ss. 121A and 124A inserted; s. 124A substituted by Act 4 of 1898.
Adaptation Orders (1937, 1948, 1950, 1956) — 'Queen', 'Governor General', 'Rajpramukh' etc. replaced or omitted.
metadata.case_query: A group stockpiles rifles and ammunition in a forest with the declared aim of seizing power in a district and ousting the State Government by force; the police arrest them before any attack. They argue they have only been planning and have not waged war.

sections.heading: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against the Government of India
sections.text: Whoever wages war against the Government of India, or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Waging war against the Government of India; OR
Attempting to wage such war; OR
Abetting the waging of such war
sections.key_principle: Waging war means organised armed rebellion against the Government with the object of overthrowing it or defying its authority — not mere riot or disorder. Attempt and abetment attract the same punishment as the principal act.

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A joins an insurrection against the Government of India. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: Joining an armed insurrection against the Government is waging war.

sections.amendment_note: 'and shall also be liable to fine' substituted for 'and shall forfeit all his property' by Act 16 of 1921, s. 2; 'transportation for life' replaced by 'imprisonment for life' by Act 26 of 1955.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).
Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen'.
Subs. by Act 16 of 1921, s. 2, for 'and shall forfeit all his property'.
Subs. by Act 36 of 1957, s. 3 and the Second Sch., for 'Illustrations'.
The brackets and letter '(a)' omitted by s. 3 and the Second Sch., ibid.
Illustration (b) omitted, by the A.O. 1950.

sections.heading: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121
sections.text: Whoever within or without India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 121, or conspires to overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Conspiracy (within or outside India)
To commit any offence under s. 121; OR
To overawe the Central or a State Government by criminal force or show of criminal force
sections.key_principle: Special conspiracy provision overriding s. 120B. No overt act is required — the agreement itself is the offence.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: To constitute a conspiracy under this section, it is not necessary that any act or illegal omission shall take place in pursuance thereof.
explanations.plain_language: Unlike s. 120A for non-offence conspiracies, no act beyond the agreement is needed.

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 27 of 1870, s. 4.
The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.
The words 'or to deprive the Queen of the sovereignty of the Provinces or of any part thereof' omitted by the A.O. 1950.
Subs. by the A.O. 1937, for 'the G. of I, or any l. G'.
Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Provincial'.
The words 'or the Government of Burma' omitted by the A.O. 1948.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life or any shorter term' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).
Ins. by Act 16 of 1921, s. 3.

sections.heading: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against the Government of India
sections.text: Whoever collects men, arms or ammunition or otherwise prepares to wage war with the intention of either waging or being prepared to wage war against the Government of India, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Collects men, arms or ammunition, or otherwise prepares to wage war
With intention of waging, or being prepared to wage, war against the Government of India
sections.key_principle: Punishes preparation (not mere planning) for waging war — an offence that falls short of an attempt under s. 121.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 16 of 1921, s. 2, for 'and shall forfeit all his property'.

sections.heading: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
sections.text: Whoever by any act, or by any illegal omission, conceals the existence of a design to wage war against the Government of India, intending by such concealment to facilitate, or knowing it to be likely that such concealment will facilitate, the waging of such war, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Conceals the existence of a design to wage war against the Government of India
By act or illegal omission
Intending or knowing it likely to facilitate the waging of war
sections.key_principle: Misprision-type offence: active concealment (or illegal omission to disclose) of a design to wage war.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen'.

sections.heading: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power
sections.text: Whoever, with the intention of inducing or compelling the President of India, or Governor of any State, to exercise or refrain from exercising in any manner any of the lawful powers of such President or Governor, assaults or wrongfully restrains, or attempts wrongfully to restrain, or overawes, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, or attempts so to overawe, such President or Governor, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Intention of inducing or compelling the President or a Governor to exercise or refrain from exercising a lawful power
Assaults, wrongfully restrains (or attempts), or overawes (or attempts to overawe) by criminal force or show of criminal force
sections.key_principle: Protects the constitutional heads of State from coercion; the specific intent to influence the exercise of a lawful power is essential.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the ibid. (A.O. 1950), for 'Governor General'.
Subs. by Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., for 'Governor'.
The words 'or Rajpramukh' omitted by the A.O. 1956.
Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Province' which had been subs. by the A.O. 1937, for 'Presidency'.
The words 'or a Lieutenant-Governor' omitted by the A.O. 1937.
The words 'or a Member of the Council of the Governor General of India' omitted by the A.O. 1948.
The words 'or of the Council of any Presidency' omitted by the A.O. 1937.
The words 'Governor General, Governor, Lieutenant-Governor or Member of Council' have successively been amended by the A.O. 1937, the A.O. 1948 and the A.O. 1950 to read as above.

sections.heading: Sedition
sections.text: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards, the Government established by law in India, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment which may extend to three years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.
sections.inserted_by: Act 27 of 1870, s. 5; substituted by Act 4 of 1898, s. 4
ingredients: Words (spoken/written), signs, visible representation or otherwise
Brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection
Towards the Government established by law in India

punishment_options.condition: Up to three years; fine may be added

sections.key_principle: Sedition requires words or acts with a tendency to incite violence or disorder (Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar, 1962); mere criticism of Government is protected. Constitutional status: in S.G. Vombatkere v. Union of India (11 May 2022) the Supreme Court directed that the provision be kept in abeyance pending re-examination. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 has no direct sedition provision (see its s. 152 on acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India).

explanations.label: Explanation 1
explanations.text: The expression "disaffection" includes disloyalty and all feelings of enmity.
explanations.plain_language: Disaffection means disloyalty or enmity towards the Government.

explanations.label: Explanation 2
explanations.text: Comments expressing disapprobation of the measures of the Government with a view to obtain their alteration by lawful means, without exciting or attempting to excite hatred, contempt or disaffection, do not constitute an offence under this section.
explanations.plain_language: Criticism of Government measures aimed at lawful change is not sedition.

explanations.label: Explanation 3
explanations.text: Comments expressing disapprobation of the administrative or other action of the Government without exciting or attempting to excite hatred, contempt or disaffection, do not constitute an offence under this section.
explanations.plain_language: Criticism of administrative action is not sedition if it does not excite hatred, contempt or disaffection.

sections.amendment_note: 'imprisonment for life' substituted for 'transportation for life or any shorter term' by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 27 of 1870, s. 5 and subs. by Act 4 of 1898, s. 4, for s. 124A.
The words 'Her Majesty or' omitted by the A.O. 1950. The words 'or the Crown Representative' ins. after the word 'Majesty' by the A.O. 1937 were omitted by the A.O. 1948.
The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.
The words 'or British Burma' ins. by the A.O. 1937 and omitted by the A.O. 1948.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life or any shorter term' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.constitutional_status: Kept in abeyance by the Supreme Court — S.G. Vombatkere v. Union of India (order dated 11-05-2022); validity upheld earlier in Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar (1962) subject to the 'tendency to incite violence' reading.

sections.heading: Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with the Government of India
sections.text: Whoever wages war against the Government of any Asiatic Power in alliance or at peace with the Government of India or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.
ingredients: Waging war against the Government of an Asiatic Power in alliance or at peace with India; OR
Attempting to wage such war; OR
Abetting the waging of such war

punishment_options.condition: Up to seven years; fine may be added

sections.key_principle: Protects India's friendly relations with neighbouring (Asiatic) allied or peaceful Powers; discretionary punishment from fine only to life imprisonment.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen'.

sections.heading: Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with the Government of India
sections.text: Whoever commits depredation, or makes preparations to commit depredation, on the territories of any Power in alliance or at peace with the Government of India, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine and to forfeiture of any property used or intended to be used in committing such depredation, or acquired by such depredation.
ingredients: Commits depredation (plunder/raid), or makes preparations to commit it
On the territory of a Power in alliance or at peace with India

punishment_options.condition: Property used, intended to be used, or acquired by the depredation

sections.key_principle: Raids on friendly territory and preparation therefor are punishable; forfeiture of property attaches to both instruments and proceeds.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen'.

sections.heading: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126
sections.text: Whoever receives any property knowing the same to have been taken in the commission of any of the offences mentioned in sections 125 and 126, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine and to forfeiture of the property so received.
ingredients: Receives property
Knowing it was taken in the commission of an offence under s. 125 or 126
sections.key_principle: Receiving-of-booty offence tied to ss. 125 and 126; knowledge is essential.

sections.heading: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of state or war to escape
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant and having the custody of any State prisoner or prisoner of war, voluntarily allows such prisoner to escape from any place in which such prisoner is confined, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
Has custody of a State prisoner or prisoner of war
Voluntarily allows such prisoner to escape
sections.key_principle: Voluntary (intentional) escape by a custodian public servant; negligent escape is dealt with in s. 129.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant and having the custody of any State prisoner or prisoner of war, negligently suffers such prisoner to escape from any place of confinement in which such prisoner is confined, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
Has custody of a State prisoner or prisoner of war
Negligently suffers the prisoner to escape
sections.key_principle: Negligence (not intention) in guarding the prisoner — milder than s. 128.

sections.heading: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner
sections.text: Whoever knowingly aids or assists any State prisoner or prisoner of war in escaping from lawful custody, or rescues or attempts to rescue any such prisoner, or harbours or conceals any such prisoner who has escaped from lawful custody, or offers or attempts to offer any resistance to the recapture of such prisoner, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Knowingly aids or assists a State prisoner/prisoner of war to escape from lawful custody; OR
Rescues or attempts to rescue; OR
Harbours or conceals an escaped prisoner; OR
Offers or attempts to offer resistance to recapture
sections.key_principle: Third-party assistance to escaped State/war prisoners. The harbouring limb does not apply to harbouring by the prisoner's husband or wife (s. 52A).

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: A State prisoner or prisoner of war, who is permitted to be at large on his parole within certain limits in India, is said to escape from lawful custody if he goes beyond the limits within which he is allowed to be at large.
explanations.plain_language: A parolee escapes custody by going beyond the permitted limits.

footnotes.note_text: The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

chapters_covered: VII — Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
key_themes: Abetting mutiny and seducing armed-forces personnel (ss. 131–132)
Abetment of assault on superior officers (ss. 133–134)
Desertion — abetment, harbouring, merchant vessel master's liability (ss. 135–137)
Abetment of insubordination (s. 138)
Service personnel carved out — tried under service laws (s. 139)
Personation of servicemen by uniform/token (s. 140)
notable_amendments: Act 10 of 1927, s. 2 — 'Army' references extended to 'Navy or Air Force'.
Act 35 of 1934 — 'sailor' inserted; s. 138A repealed.
Act 26 of 1955 — 'transportation for life' → 'imprisonment for life' in ss. 131–132.
Army, Naval and Air Force Acts replaced by the Army Act, 1950, Navy Act, 1957 and Air Force Act, 1950.
metadata.case_query: A civilian shopkeeper provides shelter for three weeks to a soldier he knows has absconded from his unit, saying he only wanted to help a friend; the prosecution charges him for harbouring a deserter.

sections.heading: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty
sections.text: Whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India or attempts to seduce any such officer, soldier, sailor or airman from his allegiance or his duty, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Abets mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman of the Indian armed forces; OR
Attempts to seduce such a person from allegiance or duty
sections.key_principle: Applies to civilians and others who induce mutiny or disloyalty in the armed forces.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: In this section the words "officer", "soldier", "sailor" and "airman" include any person subject to the Army Act, the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950), the Naval Discipline Act, the Indian Navy (Discipline) Act, 1934 (34 of 1934), the Air Force Act or the Air Force Act, 1950 (45 of 1950), as the case may be.
explanations.plain_language: The service ranks include any person subject to the respective service discipline Acts.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen'.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).
Subs. by Act 10 of 1927, s. 2 and the First Sch., for 'and Navy'.
Subs. by s. 2 and the First Sch., ibid., for 'or sailor'.
Subs. by s. 2 and the First Sch., ibid., for 'or Navy'.
Ins. by Act 27 of 1870, s. 6.
Subs. by Act 10 of 1927, s. 2 and the First Sch., for 'and soldier'.
Ins. by Act 35 of 1934, s. 2 and Sch.

sections.heading: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
sections.text: Whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, shall, if mutiny be committed in consequence of that abetment, be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Abets mutiny by a member of the armed forces
Mutiny is committed in consequence of the abetment
sections.key_principle: Aggravated form of s. 131 where mutiny actually results.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen'.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office
sections.text: Whoever abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, on any superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Abets an assault by a member of the armed forces
On a superior officer
Superior officer is in the execution of his office
sections.key_principle: Unsuccessful abetment of assault on a superior officer — compare s. 134 where the assault is committed.

sections.heading: Abetment of such assault, if the assault committed
sections.text: Whoever abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, on any superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall, if such assault be committed in consequence of that abetment be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Abets an assault by a member of the armed forces on a superior officer in execution of his office
Assault is committed in consequence of the abetment
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 133 — assault actually committed.

sections.heading: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
sections.text: Whoever abets the desertion of any officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Abets the desertion of a member of the armed forces
sections.key_principle: Abetment of desertion is punishable whether or not the desertion occurs.

sections.heading: Harbouring deserter
sections.text: Whoever, except as hereinafter excepted, knowing or having reason to believe that an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, has deserted, harbours such officer, soldier, sailor or airman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine or with both.
ingredients: Knowing or having reason to believe a member of the armed forces has deserted
Harbours such deserter
sections.key_principle: Harbouring is defined in s. 52A. Knowledge or reason to believe of desertion is essential.
exceptions: This provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour is given by a wife to her husband.

sections.heading: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
sections.text: The master or person in charge of a merchant vessel, on board of which any deserter from the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India is concealed, shall, though ignorant of such concealment, be liable to a penalty not exceeding five hundred rupees, if he might have known of such concealment but for some neglect of his duty as such master or person in charge, or but for some want of discipline on board of the vessel.
ingredients: Offender is the master or person in charge of a merchant vessel
A deserter from the Indian armed forces is concealed on board
He was ignorant of it but might have known but for neglect of duty or want of discipline
sections.key_principle: Liability for negligence (constructive knowledge) of the ship's master — only a monetary penalty.

sections.heading: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
sections.text: Whoever abets what he knows to be an act of insubordination by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force, of the Government of India, shall, if such act of insubordination be committed in consequence of that abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Abets what he knows to be an act of insubordination by a member of the armed forces
The act of insubordination is committed in consequence of the abetment
sections.key_principle: Abettor must know the act is insubordination; the offence is complete only if the insubordination is committed.

sections.heading: Application of foregoing sections to the Indian Marine Service
sections.text: [Application of foregoing sections to the Indian Marine Service.] Rep. by the Amending Act, 1934 (35 of 1934), s. 2 and Sch.
sections.repealed_by: Amending Act, 1934 (35 of 1934), s. 2 and Sch.
sections.key_principle: Repealed in 1934.

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 14 of 1887, s. 79.

sections.heading: Persons subject to certain Acts
sections.text: No person subject to the Army Act, the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950), the Naval Discipline Act, the Indian Navy (Discipline) Act, 1934 (34 of 1934), the Air Force Act or the Air Force Act, 1950 (45 of 1950), is subject to punishment under this Code for any of the offences defined in this Chapter.
ingredients: Persons subject to the Army, Naval or Air Force service discipline Acts
Not punishable under this Code for the offences defined in Chapter VII
sections.key_principle: Service personnel are tried under their own service law for these offences; the Chapter targets civilians and others outside service discipline.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 10 of 1927, s. 2 and the First Sch., for 'any Articles of War for the Army of Navy of the Queen, or for any part of such Army or Navy'.
Subs. by Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., for 'the Indian Army Act, 1911'.
Ins. by Act 35 of 1934, s. 2 and the Sch.
The words 'or that Act as modified by' omitted by the A.O. 1950.
Now see the Navy Act, 1957 (62 of 1957).
Subs. by Act 14 of 1932, s. 130 and Sch., for 'or the Air Force Act'.
Subs. by Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., for 'the Indian Air Force Act, 1932'.

sections.heading: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
sections.text: Whoever, not being a soldier, sailor or airman in the Military, Naval or Air service of the Government of India, wears any garb or carries any token resembling any garb or token used by such a soldier, sailor or airman with the intention that it may be believed that he is such a soldier, sailor or airman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Not a soldier, sailor or airman of the Indian forces
Wears a garb or carries a token resembling that used by such personnel
With the intention that he may be believed to be such a person
sections.key_principle: Personation of armed-forces personnel by uniform or token — intention to be believed to be a serviceman is essential.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 10 of 1927, s. 2 and the First Sch., for 'or sailor'.
Subs. by s. 2 and the First Sch., ibid., for 'or Naval'.
Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen'.

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity

chapters_covered: VIII — Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
key_themes: Unlawful assembly — five or more persons with an unlawful common object; membership and punishments (ss. 141–145)
Rioting and aggravated rioting (ss. 146–148)
Vicarious liability of every member for offences in prosecution of the common object (s. 149)
Hiring persons for unlawful assemblies (ss. 150, 157, 158)
Dispersal offences (ss. 145, 151) and obstructing public servants (s. 152)
Provocation to riot (s. 153)
Communal harmony and national integration offences (ss. 153A, 153AA, 153B)
Landowner/beneficiary/agent liability for riots (ss. 154–156)
Affray (ss. 159–160)
notable_amendments: Act 35 of 1969 — s. 153A substituted; Act 31 of 1972 — clause (c) of s. 153A and s. 153B inserted.
Act 25 of 2005, s. 44 — s. 153AA inserted (w.e.f. 23-6-2005).
Uttar Pradesh Act 35 of 1979 (as amended in 2016 and 2018) — abatement of trials for fine-only offences including s. 160 IPC.
metadata.case_query: Around fifty villagers gather peacefully outside a factory to protest, but when the police ask them to disperse some members start throwing stones, and a policeman is killed. One protester who stood at the back and never threw anything says he cannot be convicted of murder.

sections.heading: Unlawful assembly
sections.text: An assembly of five or more persons is designated an "unlawful assembly", if the common object of the persons composing that assembly is— First.—To overawe by criminal force, or show of criminal force, the Central or any State Government or Parliament or the Legislature of any State, or any public servant in the exercise of the lawful power of such public servant; or Second.—To resist the execution of any law, or of any legal process; or Third.—To commit any mischief or criminal trespass, or other offence; or Fourth.—By means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to any person, to take or obtain possession of any property, or to deprive any person of the enjoyment of a right of way, or of the use of water or other incorporeal right of which he is in possession or enjoyment, or to enforce any right or supposed right; or Fifth.—By means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to compel any person to do what he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do what he is legally entitled to do.
ingredients: Assembly of five or more persons
Common object is one of the five unlawful objects

clauses.text: To overawe by criminal force, or show of criminal force, the Central or any State Government or Parliament or the Legislature of any State, or any public servant in the exercise of the lawful power of such public servant.
To resist the execution of any law, or of any legal process.
To commit any mischief or criminal trespass, or other offence.

By means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to any person, to take or obtain possession of any property, or to deprive any person of the enjoyment of a right of way, or of the use of water or other incorporeal right of which he is in possession or enjoyment, or to enforce any right or supposed right.
By means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to compel any person to do what he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do what he is legally entitled to do.

sections.key_principle: Five essentials: (1) five or more persons; (2) a common object; (3) the object is one of the five specified; (4) the assembly's character is determined by its common object, not by its size alone; (5) an assembly lawful at the start can turn unlawful. Common object may be formed on the spot and is gathered from conduct, weapons and surrounding circumstances.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: An assembly which was not unlawful when it assembled, may subsequently become an unlawful assembly.
explanations.plain_language: A peaceful gathering can become unlawful if a prohibited common object develops.

footnotes.note_text: Subs., ibid. (A.O. 1950), for 'the Central or any Provincial Government or Legislature'.

sections.heading: Being member of unlawful assembly
sections.text: Whoever, being aware of facts which render any assembly an unlawful assembly, intentionally joins that assembly, or continues in it, is said to be a member of an unlawful assembly.
ingredients: Awareness of facts that make the assembly unlawful
Intentionally joins the assembly; OR intentionally continues in it
sections.key_principle: Membership requires knowledge of the unlawful character of the assembly and intentional joining or continuing — mere presence is not enough.

sections.heading: Punishment for being member of unlawful assembly
sections.text: Whoever is a member of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Is a member of an unlawful assembly (s. 142)
sections.key_principle: Basic punishment for membership of an unlawful assembly; cognizable and bailable.

sections.heading: Joining unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapon
sections.text: Whoever, being armed with any deadly weapon, or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, is a member of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Member of an unlawful assembly
Armed with a deadly weapon or anything likely to cause death when used as a weapon of offence
sections.key_principle: Aggravated membership — the weapon is carried by the offender himself.

sections.heading: Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse
sections.text: Whoever joins or continues in an unlawful assembly, knowing that such unlawful assembly has been commanded in the manner prescribed by law to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Joins or continues in an unlawful assembly
Knows it has been lawfully commanded to disperse
sections.key_principle: Defiance of a lawful dispersal order (Cr.P.C. s. 129).

sections.heading: Rioting
sections.text: Whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly, or by any member thereof, in prosecution of the common object of such assembly, every member of such assembly is guilty of the offence of rioting.
ingredients: Unlawful assembly
Force or violence used by the assembly or any member
In prosecution of the common object
Every member is guilty
sections.key_principle: Rioting = unlawful assembly + use of force or violence in pursuance of the common object. Even slight force suffices; every member is vicariously guilty.

sections.heading: Punishment for rioting
sections.text: Whoever is guilty of rioting, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Guilty of rioting (s. 146)
sections.key_principle: Basic punishment for rioting.

sections.heading: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
sections.text: Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Guilty of rioting
Armed with a deadly weapon or anything likely to cause death when used as a weapon of offence
sections.key_principle: Aggravated rioting — personal possession of a deadly weapon.

sections.heading: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
sections.text: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of the committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence.
ingredients: Offence committed by a member of an unlawful assembly
In prosecution of the common object; OR such as members knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of it
Accused was a member of the assembly at the time
sections.key_principle: Vicarious (constructive) liability based on membership, not on common intention (compare s. 34). Requires five or more persons. Two limbs: (i) offence in prosecution of the common object; (ii) offence members knew to be likely. Membership at the time of the offence is essential.

sections.heading: Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly
sections.text: Whoever hires or engages, or employs, or promotes, or connives at the hiring, engagement or employment of any person to join or become a member of any unlawful assembly, shall be punishable as a member of such unlawful assembly, and for any offence which may be committed by any such person as a member of such unlawful assembly in pursuance of such hiring, engagement or employment, in the same manner as if he had been a member of such unlawful assembly, or himself had committed such offence.
ingredients: Hires, engages, employs or promotes (or connives at the hiring of) a person
To join or become a member of an unlawful assembly

punishment_options.type: Same as a member of the unlawful assembly

punishment_options.condition: For offences committed by the hired person in pursuance of the hiring

sections.key_principle: Instigators who hire members are as liable as members — and for offences the hired persons commit in pursuance of the hiring.

sections.heading: Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse
sections.text: Whoever knowingly joins or continues in any assembly of five or more persons likely to cause a disturbance of the public peace, after such assembly has been lawfully commanded to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Assembly of five or more persons likely to cause a disturbance of the public peace
Lawfully commanded to disperse
Knowingly joins or continues
sections.key_principle: Applies to assemblies likely to disturb the peace even if their object is not an s. 141 object.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: If the assembly is an unlawful assembly within the meaning of section 141, the offender will be punishable under section 145.
explanations.plain_language: If the assembly is unlawful under s. 141, s. 145 (not s. 151) applies.

sections.heading: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.
sections.text: Whoever assaults or threatens to assault, or obstructs or attempts to obstruct, any public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, in endeavouring to disperse an unlawful assembly, or to suppress a riot or affray, or uses, or threatens, or attempts to use criminal force to such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Assaults/threatens to assault, obstructs/attempts to obstruct, or uses/threatens/attempts criminal force
On a public servant
In the discharge of duty while endeavouring to disperse an unlawful assembly or suppress a riot or affray
sections.key_principle: Special protection for public servants dispersing assemblies or suppressing riots/affrays.

sections.heading: Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot — if rioting be committed; if not committed
sections.text: Whoever malignantly, or wantonly by doing anything which is illegal, gives provocation to any person intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause the offence of rioting to be committed, shall, if the offence of rioting be committed in consequence of such provocation, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both; and if the offence of rioting be not committed, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Malignantly or wantonly doing an illegal act
Gives provocation to any person
Intending or knowing it likely that rioting will result

punishment_options.condition: Up to one year, or fine, or both — if rioting is committed
Up to six months, or fine, or both — if rioting is not committed

sections.key_principle: Two-tier punishment depending on whether rioting actually results. The provocation must be by an illegal act.

sections.heading: Promoting enmity between different groups on ground of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony
sections.text: (1) Whoever— (a) by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations or otherwise, promotes or attempts to promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, disharmony or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, or (b) commits any act which is prejudicial to the maintenance of harmony between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, and which disturbs or is likely to disturb the public tranquility, or (c) organizes any exercise, movement, drill or other similar activity intending that the participants in such activity shall use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be likely that the participants in such activity will use or be trained to use criminal force or violence, or participates in such activity intending to use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be likely that the participants in such activity will use or be trained to use criminal force or violence, against any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community and such activity for any reason whatsoever causes or is likely to cause fear or alarm or a feeling of insecurity amongst members of such religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. (2) Offence committed in place of worship, etc.—Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.inserted_by: Substituted by Act 35 of 1969, s. 2; clause (c) inserted by Act 31 of 1972, s. 2
ingredients: (1)(a) Words/signs/visible representations promoting disharmony, enmity, hatred or ill-will between groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste, community or any other ground; OR
(1)(b) Act prejudicial to harmony between groups that disturbs or is likely to disturb public tranquillity; OR
(1)(c) Organising or participating in drills/movements intending or knowing that participants will use criminal force or violence against a group, causing fear, alarm or insecurity

punishment_options.condition: Up to three years, or fine, or both — sub-section (1)
Up to five years and fine — sub-section (2), where the offence is committed in a place of worship or at a religious assembly

sections.key_principle: Hate-speech / communal harmony offence. Limb (a) requires promotion of enmity between groups (mens rea: intention to promote disharmony); limb (b) is an act likely to disturb public tranquillity; limb (c) targets organised violent drills. Aggravated in places of worship.

subsections.heading: Promoting enmity; acts prejudicial to harmony; organising violent drills
subsections.punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both

subsections.heading: Offence committed in place of worship, etc.
subsections.punishment: Imprisonment up to five years and fine

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 35 of 1969, s. 2, for section 153A (clause (c) and 'or' inserted by Act 31 of 1972, s. 2).

sections.heading: Punishment for knowingly carrying arms in any procession or organising, or holding or taking part in any mass drill or mass training with arms
sections.text: Whoever knowingly carries arms in any procession or organizes or holds or takes part in any mass drill or mass training with arms in any public place in contravention of any public notice or order issued or made under section 144A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.
ingredients: Knowingly carries arms in a procession, or organises/holds/takes part in a mass drill or training with arms
In a public place
In contravention of a notice or order under s. 144A Cr.P.C.
sections.key_principle: Armed processions and mass arms drills in violation of Cr.P.C. s. 144A orders. 'Arms' includes firearms, sharp-edged weapons, lathis, dandas and sticks.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: "Arms" means articles of any description designed or adapted as weapons for offence or defence and includes firearms, sharp edged weapons, lathis, dandas and sticks.
explanations.plain_language: 'Arms' covers firearms, bladed weapons and even lathis and sticks.

sections.heading: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration
sections.text: (1) Whoever, by words either spoken or written or by signs or by visible representations or otherwise,— (a) makes or publishes any imputation that any class of persons cannot, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, or (b) asserts, counsels, advises, propagates or publishes that any class of persons shall, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, be denied, or deprived of their rights as citizens of India, or (c) makes or publishes any assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. (2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: (1)(a) Imputation that a class of persons cannot bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution or uphold India's sovereignty and integrity; OR
(1)(b) Assertion/advice that a class of persons shall be denied or deprived of their rights as citizens; OR
(1)(c) Assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning a class's obligation, causing or likely to cause disharmony, enmity, hatred or ill-will

punishment_options.condition: Up to three years, or fine, or both — sub-section (1)
Up to five years and fine — sub-section (2), place of worship or religious assembly

sections.key_principle: Protects national integration by punishing speech that casts doubt on a group's loyalty or denies citizenship rights. Aggravated in places of worship.

subsections.heading: Imputations/assertions prejudicial to national integration
subsections.punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both

subsections.heading: Offence in place of worship, etc.
subsections.punishment: Imprisonment up to five years and fine

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 31 of 1972, s. 2.

sections.heading: Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held
sections.text: Whenever any unlawful assembly or riot takes place, the owner or occupier of the land upon which such unlawful assembly is held, or such riot is committed, and any person having or claiming an interest in such land, shall be punishable with fine not exceeding one thousand rupees, if he or his agent or manager, knowing that such offence is being or has been committed, or having reason to believe it is likely to be committed, do not give the earliest notice thereof in his or their power to the principal officer at the nearest police-station, and do not, in the case of his or their having reason to believe that it was about to be committed, use all lawful means in his or their power to prevent it and, in the event of its taking place, do not use all lawful means in his or their power to disperse or suppress the riot or unlawful assembly.
ingredients: Unlawful assembly or riot takes place on land
Offender is the owner, occupier or person claiming an interest in the land
He or his agent/manager knew or had reason to believe, and failed to give earliest notice to the police
Failed to use all lawful means to prevent, disperse or suppress
sections.key_principle: Duty on landowners/occupiers to notify the police and act against riots or unlawful assemblies on their land.

sections.heading: Liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed
sections.text: Whenever a riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of any person who is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place or who claims any interest in such land, or in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot, or who has accepted or derived any benefit therefrom, such person shall be punishable with fine, if he or his agent or manager, having reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed or that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held, shall not respectively use all lawful means in his or their power to prevent such assembly or riot from taking place, and for suppressing and dispersing the same.
ingredients: Riot committed for the benefit of, or on behalf of, a person with an interest in the land/dispute, or who derived benefit
He or his agent/manager had reason to believe the riot was likely
Failed to use all lawful means to prevent, suppress and disperse
sections.key_principle: Beneficiaries of riots are liable to fine if they fail to use lawful means to prevent them.

sections.heading: Liability of agent of owner or occupier for whose benefit riot is committed
sections.text: Whenever a riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of any person who is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place, or who claims any interest in such land, or in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot, or who has accepted or derived any benefit therefrom, the agent or manager of such person shall be punishable with fine, if such agent or manager, having reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed, or that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held, shall not use all lawful means in his power to prevent such riot or assembly from taking place and for suppressing and dispersing the same.
ingredients: Riot committed for the benefit of a person described in s. 155
Offender is that person's agent or manager
Had reason to believe riot was likely and failed to use all lawful means to prevent and disperse
sections.key_principle: Extends s. 155 liability to the beneficiary's agent or manager.

sections.heading: Harbouring persons hired for an unlawful assembly
sections.text: Whoever harbours, receives or assembles, in any house or premises in his occupation or charge, or under his control any persons knowing that such persons have been hired, engaged or employed, or are about to be hired, engaged or employed, to join or become members of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Harbours, receives or assembles persons in premises in his occupation, charge or control
Knows they have been (or are about to be) hired to join an unlawful assembly
sections.key_principle: Knowledge that the persons are hired for an unlawful assembly is essential. 'Harbour' is defined in s. 52A.

sections.heading: Being hired to take part in an unlawful assembly or riot
sections.text: Whoever is engaged, or hired, or offers or attempts to be hired or engaged, to do or assist in doing any of the acts specified in section 141, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both, or to go armed.—and whoever, being so engaged or hired as aforesaid, goes armed, or engages or offers to go armed, with any deadly weapon or with anything which used as a weapon of offence is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Is engaged or hired, or offers/attempts to be hired or engaged, to do or assist in any act specified in s. 141
(Aggravated) goes armed, or engages/offers to go armed, with a deadly weapon

punishment_options.condition: Up to six months, or fine, or both
Up to two years, or fine, or both — if hired to go armed

sections.key_principle: Targets the hired participants themselves (compare s. 150 for those who hire them).

sections.heading: Affray
sections.text: When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to "commit an affray".
ingredients: Two or more persons
Fighting
In a public place
Disturbing the public peace
sections.key_principle: Affray requires actual fighting in public that disturbs the peace — contrast with rioting (five or more, common object) and assault.

sections.heading: Punishment for committing affray
sections.text: Whoever commits an affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Commits an affray (s. 159)
sections.key_principle: Mild punishment for affray; the least serious public-tranquillity offence in the Chapter.

state_amendments.text: Abatement of certain trials. Notwithstanding anything in any other law for the time being in force, (1) the trial of an accused for (a) an offence punishable under (i) the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988; (ii) the Public Gambling Act, 1867, not being an offence punishable under section 3 of that Act or an offence in respect of wagering punishable under section 13 of that Act; (iii) section 34 of the Police Act, 1861; or (iv) section 160 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860; or (b) any other offence punishable with fine only, or (2) a procedure under section 107 or section 109 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, pending before a Magistrate on the date of commencement of this Act from before 'December 31, 2015', shall abate.
state_amendments.authority: Uttar Pradesh Act 35 of 1979, s. 9, as amended by U.P. Act 29 of 2016 and 9 of 2018

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants

chapters_covered: IX — Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
key_themes: Gratification offences (ss. 161–165A) — all repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Public servant disobeying the law causing injury (s. 166)
Public servant failing to register FIRs for specified crimes against women (s. 166A); hospital non-treatment of victims (s. 166B)
Incorrect documents by public servants (s. 167)
Public servants engaging in trade or buying/bidding for property (ss. 168–169)
Personation and uniform/token offences (ss. 170–171)
notable_amendments: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31 — ss. 161–165A repealed.
Act 13 of 2013, s. 3 — ss. 166A and 166B inserted (w.e.f. 3-2-2013).
Act 22 of 2018, s. 2 — list of offences in s. 166A(c) amended (w.e.f. 21-4-2018).
Act 21 of 2000 — 'electronic record' added in s. 167.
State amendments: Kerala (s. 161), Arunachal Pradesh (s. 166A).
metadata.case_query: A police officer refuses to register an FIR for an alleged gang rape reported by a woman, telling her to settle the matter with the accused's family; he claims he only wanted to avoid unnecessary litigation.

sections.heading: Public servant taking a gratification other than legal remuneration, in respect of an official act
sections.text: [Public servant taking a gratification other than legal remuneration, in respect of an official act.] Rep. by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31.
sections.repealed_by: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31.
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31.

state_amendments.text: In section 161, after the explanation relating to 'A motive or reward for doing', an explanation defining 'Public Servant' (for ss. 161, 162, 163, 164, 165 and 165A) is inserted to include, besides s. 21 public servants: (i) every officer in the service or pay of the Travancore Devaswom Board or the Cochin Devaswom Board; (ii) every officer in the service or pay and every member of the Wakfs Board constituted under the Wakfs Act, 1954; (iii) the President and every member of a Village Court or Village Panchayat Court; (iv) every member of the Board of Directors or of the executive or managing committee and every officer or servant of a registered co-operative society; (v) every member of the governing body and every officer or servant of a society registered under the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 or the Societies Registration Act, 1860, receiving Government aid or grant; (vi) every teacher or other officer or servant of the University of Kerala; (vii) every examiner of a University or Government Examination; (viii) every Manager, teacher or servant of an educational institution which receives or has received Government or University of Kerala aid or grant.

sections.heading: Taking a gratification, in order, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence a public servant
sections.text: [Taking a gratification, in order, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence a public servant.] Rep. by s. 31, ibid.
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, s. 31

sections.heading: Taking a gratification for the exercise of personal influence with a public servant
sections.text: [Taking a gratification for the exercise of personal influence with a public servant.] Rep. by s. 31, ibid.
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, s. 31

sections.heading: Punishment for abetment by public servant of the offences above defined
sections.text: [Punishment for abetment by public servant of the offences above defined.] Rep. by s. 31, ibid.
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, s. 31

sections.heading: Public servant obtaining any valuable thing, without consideration, from person concerned in any proceeding or business transacted by such public servant
sections.text: [Public servant obtaining any valuable thing, without consideration, from person concerned in any proceeding or business transacted by such public servant.] Rep. by s. 31, ibid.
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, s. 31

sections.heading: Punishment for abetment of offences defined in section 161 or section 165
sections.text: [Punishment for abetment of offences defined in section 161 or section 165.] Rep. by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31.
sections.repealed_by: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31

sections.heading: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will by such disobedience, cause injury to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
Knowingly disobeys a direction of the law as to how he is to conduct himself
Intending to cause, or knowing it likely to cause, injury to any person
sections.key_principle: Wilful disobedience of a legal duty by a public servant that injures a person. 'Injury' has the s. 44 meaning.

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A, being an officer directed by law to take property in execution, in order to satisfy a decree pronounced in Z's favour by a Court of Justice, knowingly disobeys that direction of law, with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause injury to Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: Knowing disobedience of a legal duty likely to injure another is an offence.

sections.heading: Public servant disobeying direction under law
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant,— (a) knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other matter, or (b) knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation, or (c) fails to record any information given to him under sub-section (1) of section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), in relation to cognizable offence punishable under section 326A, section 326B, section 354, section 354B, section 370, section 370A, section 376, section 376A, section 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB, section 376E or section 509, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
(a) Knowingly disobeys a legal direction prohibiting him from requiring a person's attendance for investigation; OR
(b) Knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, a legal direction regulating how an investigation is conducted; OR
(c) Fails to record an FIR under s. 154(1) Cr.P.C. for specified offences against women (acid attack, sexual harassment, trafficking, rape etc.)

punishment_options.condition: Minimum six months, up to two years

sections.key_principle: Mandatory minimum six months. Clause (c) penalises police officers who refuse to register FIRs for the listed crimes against women, particularly after the Nirbhaya reforms.

state_amendments.text: In section 166A, clause (c), for the words, figures and letters 'section 326A, section 326B, section 354, section 354A, section 370, section 370A, section 376, section 376A, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376E or section 509' the following shall be substituted: 'section 326A, section 326B, section 354, sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 354A, section 354B, section 354C, sub-section (2) of section 354D, section 370, section 370A, section 376, section 376A, section 376AA, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376E or section 509'.

sections.amendment_note: Words 'section 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB' substituted by Act 22 of 2018, s. 2 (w.e.f. 21-4-2018).

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 22 of 2018, s. 2, for 'section 376B, section 376C, section 376D' (w.e.f. 21-4-2018).

sections.heading: Punishment for non-treatment of victim
sections.text: Whoever, being in charge of a hospital, public or private, whether run by the Central Government, the State Government, local bodies or any other person, contravenes the provisions of section 357C of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both.
ingredients: Offender is in charge of a hospital, public or private
Contravenes s. 357C Cr.P.C. (duty to treat victims of acid attack, rape etc. free of cost)
sections.key_principle: Penalises hospitals that refuse free treatment/first-aid to victims of the specified offences.

sections.heading: Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, and being, as such public servant, charged with the preparation or translation of any document or electronic record, frames, prepares or translates that document or electronic record in a manner which he knows or believes to be incorrect, intending thereby to cause or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause injury to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant charged with preparing or translating a document or electronic record
Frames, prepares or translates it in a manner he knows or believes to be incorrect
Intending or knowing it likely to cause injury to any person
sections.key_principle: Incorrect official documents with intent/knowledge of injury; 'electronic record' added in 2000.
sections.amendment_note: Words relating to 'electronic record' substituted by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and First Sch. (w.e.f. 17-10-2000).

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and the First Sch., for certain words (w.e.f. 17-10-2000).

sections.heading: Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound as such public servant not to engage in trade, engages in trade, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
Legally bound not to engage in trade
Engages in trade
sections.key_principle: Applies only to public servants who are legally barred from trading.

sections.heading: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound as such public servant, not to purchase or bid for certain property, purchases or bids for that property, either in his own name or in the name of another, or jointly, or in shares with others, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and the property, if purchased, shall be confiscated.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
Legally bound not to purchase or bid for certain property
Purchases or bids, in his own or another's name, jointly or in shares
sections.key_principle: Prevents officials who manage or sell property (e.g. auction officers) from benefiting; confiscation attaches to purchased property, even through benami arrangements.

sections.heading: Personating a public servant
sections.text: Whoever pretends to hold any particular office as a public servant, knowing that he does not hold such office or falsely personates any other person holding such office, and in such assumed character does or attempts to do any act under colour of such office, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Pretends to hold a public-servant office knowing he does not; OR falsely personates the holder of such office
In the assumed character does or attempts any act under colour of that office
sections.key_principle: Requires both pretence/personation AND an act (or attempt) under colour of the office.

sections.heading: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent
sections.text: Whoever, not belonging to a certain class of public servants, wears any garb or carries any token resembling any garb or token used by that class of public servants, with the intention that it may be believed, or with the knowledge that it is likely to be believed, that he belongs to that class of public servants, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Not belonging to a class of public servants
Wears the garb or carries a token resembling theirs
Intending, or knowing it likely, that he will be believed to belong to that class
sections.key_principle: Lesser offence than s. 170 — no act under colour of office is required, only the deceptive uniform/token.

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences Relating to Elections

chapters_covered: IXA — Of Offences Relating to Elections
key_themes: Definitions of 'candidate' and 'electoral right' (s. 171A)
Bribery — giving and accepting gratifications (ss. 171B, 171E); treating punished by fine only
Undue influence — threats and spiritual censure (ss. 171C, 171F)
Personation and double-voting (ss. 171D, 171F)
False statements about candidates (s. 171G); unauthorised election expenses (s. 171H); failure to keep accounts (s. 171-I)
notable_amendments: Chapter IXA inserted by Act 39 of 1920, s. 2.
Act 40 of 1975, s. 9 — definition of 'candidate' substituted.
Act 24 of 2003, s. 5 — proxy-voting proviso added to s. 171D (w.e.f. 22-9-2003).
metadata.case_query: A candidate distributes sarees and liquor to voters the night before polling, saying it is just a festival gift; he argues that it is not a reward for voting for him.

sections.heading: "Candidate", "Electoral right" defined
sections.text: For the purposes of this Chapter— (a) "candidate" means a person who has been nominated as a candidate at any election; (b) "electoral right" means the right of a person to stand, or not to stand as, or to withdraw from being, a candidate or to vote or refrain from voting at an election.
sections.inserted_by: Chapter IXA inserted by Act 39 of 1920, s. 2; clause (a) substituted by Act 40 of 1975, s. 9
ingredients: Candidate: a person nominated as a candidate at any election
Electoral right: right to stand or not stand as, or withdraw as, a candidate; or to vote or refrain from voting
sections.key_principle: Definitions for the election offences. Electoral right covers both positive and negative choices (standing, withdrawing, voting, abstaining).

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 39 of 1920, s. 2 (Chapter IXA).
Subs. by Act 40 of 1975, s. 9, for cl. (a).

sections.heading: Bribery
sections.text: (1) Whoever— (i) gives a gratification to any person with the object of inducing him or any other person to exercise any electoral right or of rewarding any person for having exercised any such right; or (ii) accepts either for himself or for any other person any gratification as a reward for exercising any such right or for inducing or attempting to induce any other person to exercise any such right, commits the offence of bribery: Provided that a declaration of public policy or a promise of public action shall not be an offence under this section. (2) A person who offers, or agrees to give, or offers or attempts to procure, a gratification shall be deemed to give a gratification. (3) A person who obtains or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain a gratification shall be deemed to accept a gratification, and a person who accepts a gratification as a motive for doing what he does not intend to do, or as a reward for doing what he has not done, shall be deemed to have accepted the gratification as a reward.
ingredients: Giving a gratification to induce or reward the exercise of an electoral right; OR
Accepting a gratification as a reward for exercising an electoral right or for inducing others
Giver: includes one who offers, agrees to give, or offers/attempts to procure
Acceptor: includes one who obtains, agrees to accept or attempts to obtain
sections.key_principle: Electoral bribery covers both giver and taker; offers and attempts are deemed giving/accepting. Election promises (public policy) are expressly excluded. Punishment under s. 171E.

subsections.text: Bribery — giving or accepting a gratification for an electoral right.
subsections.proviso: A declaration of public policy or a promise of public action is not an offence.

subsections.text: Deemed giving — offering, agreeing to give, or offering/attempting to procure a gratification.
Deemed acceptance — obtaining, agreeing to accept or attempting to obtain; also accepting as a motive for doing what one does not intend to do, or as a reward for what one has not done.

sections.heading: Undue influence at elections
sections.text: (1) Whoever voluntarily interferes or attempts to interfere with the free exercise of any electoral right commits the offence of undue influence at an election. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of sub-section (1), whoever— (a) threatens any candidate or voter, or any person in whom a candidate or voter is interested, with injury of any kind, or (b) induces or attempts to induce a candidate or voter to believe that he or any person in whom he is interested will become or will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure or of spiritual censure, shall be deemed to interfere with the free exercise of the electoral right of such candidate or voter, within the meaning of sub-section (1). (3) A declaration of public policy or a promise of public action or the mere exercise of a legal right without intent to interfere with an electoral right, shall not be deemed to be interference within the meaning of this section.
ingredients: Voluntarily interferes (or attempts to interfere) with the free exercise of an electoral right
Deemed interference: threatening a candidate/voter (or a person in whom they are interested) with injury; OR inducing belief of Divine displeasure or spiritual censure
Excluded: declarations of public policy, promises of public action, mere exercise of a legal right without intent to interfere
sections.key_principle: Undue influence is interference with the free exercise of voting/candidacy rights through threats or spiritual coercion. Appeals to religion that threaten divine displeasure fall within (2)(b). Punishment under s. 171F.

subsections.text: General offence — voluntary interference or attempted interference with the free exercise of an electoral right.
Deemed interference: (a) threat of injury of any kind to a candidate or voter or a person in whom they are interested; (b) inducing belief of Divine displeasure or spiritual censure.
Exclusion — declaration of public policy, promise of public action, or mere exercise of a legal right without intent to interfere.

sections.heading: Personation at elections
sections.text: Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper or votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or in a fictitious name, or who having voted once at such election applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name, and whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way, commits the offence of personation at an election. Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to a person who has been authorised to vote as proxy for an elector under any law for the time being in force in so far as he votes as a proxy for such elector.
sections.inserted_by: Proviso inserted by Act 24 of 2003, s. 5 (w.e.f. 22-9-2003)
ingredients: Applies for a voting paper or votes in another's name (living or dead) or a fictitious name; OR
Having voted once, applies again in his own name at the same election; OR
Abets, procures or attempts to procure voting in such ways
Not applicable to a lawfully authorised proxy voter
sections.key_principle: Impersonation voting and double voting; the abettor/procurer is equally guilty. Proxy voting (e.g. service voters) is excluded. Punishment under s. 171F.

footnotes.note_text: The proviso ins. by Act 24 of 2003, s. 5 (w.e.f. 22-9-2003).

sections.heading: Punishment for bribery
sections.text: Whoever commits the offence of bribery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both: Provided that bribery by treating shall be punished with fine only.
ingredients: Commits bribery under s. 171B
sections.key_principle: 'Treating' (food, drink, entertainment, provision) carries only a fine.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: "Treating" means that form of bribery where the gratification consists in food, drink, entertainment, or provision.
explanations.plain_language: Treating = bribing with food, drink, entertainment or provision.

sections.heading: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election
sections.text: Whoever commits the offence of undue influence or personation at an election shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Commits undue influence (s. 171C) or personation (s. 171D) at an election
sections.key_principle: Common punishment for undue influence and personation.

sections.heading: False statement in connection with an election
sections.text: Whoever with intent to affect the result of an election makes or publishes any statement purporting to be a statement of fact which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, in relation to the personal character or conduct of any candidate shall be punished with fine.
ingredients: Makes or publishes a statement purporting to be a statement of fact
False, and known/believed to be false or not believed to be true
In relation to the personal character or conduct of a candidate
With intent to affect the result of an election
