sections.key_principle: Targets false factual statements about a candidate's character or conduct (not about policy or political positions). Only a fine can be imposed.

sections.heading: Illegal payments in connection with an election
sections.text: Whoever without the general or special authority in writing of a candidate incurs or authorises expenses on account of the holding of any public meeting, or upon any advertisement, circular or publication, or in any other way whatsoever for the purpose of promoting or procuring the election of such candidate, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees: Provided that if any person having incurred any such expenses not exceeding the amount of ten rupees without authority obtains within ten days from the date on which such expenses were incurred the approval in writing of the candidate, he shall be deemed to have incurred such expenses with the authority of the candidate.
ingredients: Incurs or authorises expenses to promote or procure a candidate's election
Without the general or special written authority of the candidate
sections.key_principle: Candidates alone control campaign expenditure. Small unauthorised expenses (up to ₹10) can be ratified within ten days.

provisos.text: If any person having incurred any such expenses not exceeding ₹10 without authority obtains within ten days the written approval of the candidate, the expenses are deemed to have been incurred with authority.

sections.heading: Failure to keep election accounts
sections.text: Whoever being required by any law for the time being in force or any rule having the force of law to keep accounts of expenses incurred at or in connection with an election fails to keep such accounts shall be punished with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.
ingredients: Required by law or a rule having the force of law to keep election-expense accounts
Fails to keep such accounts
sections.key_principle: Compliance offence to support election-expenditure scrutiny.

chapters.chapter_title: Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants

chapters_covered: X — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
key_themes: Evading or obstructing legal process — absconding, preventing service, non-attendance (ss. 172–174, 174A)
Duties to produce documents and give information (ss. 175–177)
Refusals: oath, answering, signing (ss. 178–180)
False statements and information to public servants (ss. 181–182)
Resisting or obstructing property seizure/sale and illegal bidding (ss. 183–185)
Obstructing public servants and omission to assist (ss. 186–187)
Disobedience of promulgated orders — prohibitory orders (s. 188)
Threats to public servants and to persons seeking protection (ss. 189–190)
notable_amendments: Act 21 of 2000 — 'electronic record' added to ss. 172, 173, 175.
Act 3 of 1895 — s. 182 substituted; Act 3 of 1894 — Explanation to s. 177 added.
Act 22 of 1939 — last limb of s. 176 added (Cr.P.C. 1898 s. 565).
A.O. 1950 — references to 'Supreme Court' and 'Zila Judge' replaced in s. 174 illustrations.
metadata.case_query: During a declared prohibitory order against public gatherings, a man leads a rally through a banned street although police had announced the order by loudspeaker; a scuffle follows and several shops are damaged. He says he did not intend any harm.

sections.heading: Absconding to avoid service of summons or other proceeding
sections.text: Whoever absconds in order to avoid being served with a summons, notice or order proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue such summons, notice or order, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the summons or notice or order is to attend in person or by agent, or to produce a document or an electronic record in a Court of Justice, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Absconds
In order to avoid service of a summons, notice or order
Issued by a public servant legally competent to issue it

punishment_options.condition: Up to one month, or fine up to ₹500, or both
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both — if the summons requires personal/agent attendance or production of a document/electronic record in a Court of Justice

sections.key_principle: Evasion of service of legal process; the two-tier punishment depends on whether the summons relates to court attendance or production of documents.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and the First Sch., for 'produce a document in a Court of Justice' (w.e.f. 17-10-2000).

sections.heading: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof
sections.text: Whoever in any manner intentionally prevents the serving on himself, or on any other person, of any summons, notice or order proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue such summons, notice or order, or intentionally prevents the lawful affixing to any place of any such summons, notice or order, or intentionally removes any such summons, notice or order from any place to which it is lawfully affixed, or intentionally prevents the lawful making of any proclamation, under the authority of any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to direct such proclamation to be made, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent, or to produce a document or electronic record in a Court of Justice with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Intentionally prevents service of a summons/notice/order on himself or another; OR
Intentionally prevents the lawful affixing of such a document; OR
Intentionally removes such a document from where it is lawfully affixed; OR
Intentionally prevents the lawful making of a proclamation

punishment_options.condition: Up to one month, or fine up to ₹500, or both
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both — if for attendance or production of document/electronic record in court

sections.key_principle: Active obstruction of service/publication of legal process (contrast with s. 172 where the accused himself absconds).

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and the First Sch., for 'to produce a document in a Court of Justice' (w.e.f. 17-10-2000).

sections.heading: Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant
sections.text: Whoever, being legally bound to attend in person or by an agent at a certain place and time in obedience to a summons, notice, order, or proclamation proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue the same, intentionally omits to attend at that place or time, or departs from the place where he is bound to attend before the time at which it is lawful for him to depart, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent in a Court of Justice, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Legally bound to attend in person or by agent at a certain place and time
Intentionally omits to attend at that place or time, or departs before the lawful time

punishment_options.condition: Up to one month, or fine up to ₹500, or both
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both — where attendance in a Court of Justice is required

sections.key_principle: Intentional non-attendance is the gist; genuine inability is not an offence.

illustrations.label: Illustration (a)
illustrations.text: A, being legally bound to appear before the High Court at Calcutta, in obedience to a subpoena issuing from that Court, intentionally omits to appear. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: Intentional non-appearance before a court in answer to a subpoena is an offence.

illustrations.label: Illustration (b)
illustrations.text: A, being legally bound to appear before a District Judge, as a witness, in obedience to a summons issued by that District Judge intentionally omits to appear. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: A witness who intentionally fails to attend commits the offence.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Supreme Court'.
Subs. ibid., for 'Zila Judge'.

sections.heading: Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 82 of Act 2 of 1974
sections.text: Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both, and where a declaration has been made under sub-section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Failure to appear at the specified place and time
As required by a proclamation published under s. 82(1) Cr.P.C.
(Aggravated) A declaration under s. 82(4) pronouncing him a proclaimed offender has been made

punishment_options.condition: Up to three years, or fine, or both
Up to seven years and fine — if declared a proclaimed offender under s. 82(4) Cr.P.C.

sections.key_principle: Skipping a court proclamation (absconder). Higher punishment for proclaimed offenders.

sections.heading: Omission to produce document to public servant by person legally bound to produce it
sections.text: Whoever, being legally bound to produce or deliver up any document or electronic record to any public servant, as such, intentionally omits so to produce or deliver up the same, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the document or electronic record is to be produced or delivered up to a Court of Justice, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Legally bound to produce or deliver up a document or electronic record to a public servant
Intentionally omits to do so

punishment_options.condition: Up to one month, or fine up to ₹500, or both
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both — if to be produced to a Court of Justice

sections.key_principle: Intentional failure to produce documents/electronic records that one is legally bound to produce.

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A, being legally bound to produce a document before a District Court, intentionally omits to produce the same. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: Intentional refusal to produce a document one is bound to produce is an offence.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and the First Sch., for 'document' (w.e.f. 17-10-2000).
Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Zila Court'.

sections.heading: Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it
sections.text: Whoever, being legally bound to give any notice or to furnish information on any subject to any public servant, as such, intentionally omits to give such notice or to furnish such information in the manner and at the time required by law, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the notice or information required to be given respects the commission of an offence, or is required for the purpose of preventing the commission of an offence, or in order to the apprehension of an offender, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both; or, if the notice or information required to be given is required by an order passed under sub-section (1) of section 565 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (5 of 1898), with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Legally bound to give notice or furnish information to a public servant
Intentionally omits to do so in the manner and at the time required by law

punishment_options.condition: Up to one month, or fine up to ₹500, or both
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both — if the information concerns an offence, its prevention or the apprehension of an offender
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both — if required by an order under s. 565(1) Cr.P.C., 1898

sections.key_principle: Three-tier punishment depending on the importance of the information withheld. The Explanation to s. 177 defines 'offence' for this section to include certain offences committed outside India.

footnotes.note_text: Added by Act 22 of 1939, s. 2.

sections.heading: Furnishing false information
sections.text: Whoever, being legally bound to furnish information on any subject to any public servant, as such, furnishes, as true, information on the subject which he knows or has reason to believe to be false shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both; or, if the information which he is legally bound to give respects the commission of an offence, or is required for the purpose of preventing the commission of an offence, or in order to the apprehension of an offender, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.inserted_by: Explanation added by Act 3 of 1894, s. 5
ingredients: Legally bound to furnish information to a public servant
Furnishes, as true, information he knows or has reason to believe to be false

punishment_options.condition: Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both
Up to two years, or fine, or both — if the information concerns an offence, its prevention or the apprehension of an offender

sections.key_principle: False information given where one is legally bound to give information (compare s. 182, where there is no legal duty to inform).

illustrations.label: Illustration (a)
illustrations.text: A, a landholder, knowing of the commission of a murder within the limits of his estate, wilfully misinforms the Magistrate of the district that the death has occurred by accident in consequence of the bite of a snake. A is guilty of the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: A landholder legally bound to inform who gives false information commits the offence.

illustrations.label: Illustration (b)
illustrations.text: A, a village watchman, knowing that a considerable body of strangers has passed through his village in order to commit a dacoity in the house of Z, a wealthy merchant residing in a neighbouring place, and being bound under clause 5, section VII, Regulation III, 1821, of the Bengal Code, to give early and punctual information of the above fact to the officer of the nearest police-station, wilfully misinforms the police officer that a body of suspicious characters passed through the village with a view to commit dacoity in a certain distant place in a different direction. Here A is guilty of the offence defined in the latter part of this section.
illustrations.verdict: A guilty under the aggravated limb
illustrations.key_principle: False information about a planned offence by a person bound to inform attracts the higher punishment.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: In section 176 and in this section the word "offence" includes any act committed at any place out of India, which, if committed in India, would be punishable under any of the following sections, namely, 302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460; and the word "offender" includes any person who is alleged to have been guilty of any such act.
explanations.plain_language: For ss. 176–177 'offence' includes listed serious offences committed abroad that would be punishable under those IPC sections if committed in India.

footnotes.note_text: Rep. by Act 17 of 1862, s. VII and Sch.
Added by Act 3 of 1894, s. 5.
The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.

sections.heading: Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it
sections.text: Whoever refuses to bind himself by an oath or affirmation to state the truth, when required so to bind himself by a public servant legally competent to require that he shall so bind himself, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Required to bind himself by oath or affirmation by a legally competent public servant
Refuses
sections.key_principle: Refusal of the oath or affirmation itself (see s. 51 for 'oath').

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 10 of 1873, s. 15.

sections.heading: Refusing to answer public servant authorised to question
sections.text: Whoever, being legally bound to state the truth on any subject to any public servant, refuses to answer any question demanded of him touching that subject by such public servant in the exercise of the legal powers of such public servant, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Legally bound to state the truth on a subject to a public servant
Refuses to answer a question touching that subject
Question asked in the exercise of the public servant's legal powers
sections.key_principle: Compelled-answering must be within the questioner's legal powers; constitutional protection against self-incrimination (Art. 20(3)) limits its operation against accused persons.

sections.heading: Refusing to sign statement
sections.text: Whoever refuses to sign any statement made by him, when required to sign that statement by a public servant legally competent to require that he shall sign that statement, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Statement made by the accused
Required to sign by a legally competent public servant
Refuses to sign
sections.key_principle: Under Cr.P.C. s. 162 a person need not sign a police statement, so this provision has limited operation in police investigations.

sections.heading: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant or person authorised to administer an oath or affirmation
sections.text: Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or affirmation to state the truth on any subject to any public servant or other person authorized by law to administer such oath or affirmation, makes, to such public servant or other person as aforesaid, touching that subject, any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Legally bound by oath/affirmation to state the truth to a public servant or authorised person
Makes a false statement touching that subject
Knows/believes it to be false or does not believe it to be true
sections.key_principle: False statement on oath outside a judicial proceeding (judicial perjury is dealt with in s. 193).

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 10 of 1873, s. 15.

sections.heading: False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person
sections.text: Whoever gives to any public servant any information which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, such public servant— (a) to do or omit anything which such public servant ought not to do or omit if the true state of facts respecting which such information is given were known by him, or (b) to use the lawful power of such public servant to the injury or annoyance of any person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Gives a public servant information he knows or believes to be false
Intending, or knowing it likely, that the public servant will (a) do/omit something he ought not to if the true facts were known; or (b) use his lawful power to the injury or annoyance of any person
sections.key_principle: False complaint/information to officials to misuse their power against someone. A court may take cognizance only on the complaint of the public servant concerned (Cr.P.C. s. 195).

illustrations.label: Illustration (a)
illustrations.text: A informs a Magistrate that Z, a police-officer, subordinate to such Magistrate, has been guilty of neglect of duty or misconduct, knowing such information to be false, and knowing it to be likely that the information will cause the Magistrate to dismiss Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: False information intended to cause an official to dismiss another is covered.

illustrations.label: Illustration (b)
illustrations.text: A falsely informs a public servant that Z has contraband salt in a secret place, knowing such information to be false, and knowing that it is likely that the consequence of the information will be a search of Z's premises, attended with annoyance to Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: False tip-off causing a search and annoyance is covered.

illustrations.label: Illustration (c)
illustrations.text: A falsely informs a policeman that he has been assaulted and robbed in the neighbourhood of a particular village. He does not mention the name of any person as one of his assailants, but knows it to be likely that in consequence of this information the police will make enquiries and institute searches in the village to the annoyance of the villagers or some of them. A has committed an offence under this section.
illustrations.key_principle: A false report without naming anyone is still an offence if annoyance to others is likely.

sections.amendment_note: Section substituted by Act 3 of 1895, s. 1, for original s. 182.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 3 of 1895, s. 1, for section 182.

sections.heading: Resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant
sections.text: Whoever offers any resistance to the taking of any property by the lawful authority of any public servant, knowing or having reason to believe that he is such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Offers resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant
Knowing or having reason to believe that he is a public servant
sections.key_principle: Resistance to attachments, distress and similar seizures by public servants acting lawfully.

sections.heading: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant
sections.text: Whoever intentionally obstructs any sale of property offered for sale by the lawful authority of any public servant, as such, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Intentionally obstructs a sale of property
Sale offered by the lawful authority of a public servant
sections.key_principle: Protects court/revenue auctions from obstruction.

sections.heading: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant
sections.text: Whoever, at any sale of property held by the lawful authority of a public servant, as such, purchases or bids for any property on account of any person, whether himself or any other, whom he knows to be under a legal incapacity to purchase that property at that sale, or bids for such property not intending to perform the obligations under which he lays himself by such bidding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: At a sale held by the lawful authority of a public servant
Purchases or bids on account of a person known to be under a legal incapacity to purchase; OR
Bids not intending to perform the obligations of the bid
sections.key_principle: Targets fraudulent bidding and bidding for persons barred from purchasing at official sales.

sections.heading: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions
sections.text: Whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Voluntarily obstructs a public servant
In the discharge of his public functions
sections.key_principle: Obstruction need not involve force; 'voluntarily' (s. 39) requires intent to obstruct or knowledge it is likely. Mere criticism or non-cooperation without obstruction is not enough. (Section 195 Cr.P.C. requires a complaint by the public servant to take cognizance.)

sections.heading: Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance
sections.text: Whoever, being bound by law to render or furnish assistance to any public servant in the execution of his public duty, intentionally omits to give such assistance, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both; and if such assistance be demanded of him by a public servant legally competent to make such demand for the purposes of executing any process lawfully issued by a Court of Justice, or of preventing the commission of an offence, or suppressing a riot, or affray, or of apprehending a person charged with or guilty of an offence, or of having escaped from lawful custody, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Bound by law to render assistance to a public servant in the execution of his public duty
Intentionally omits to give such assistance
(Aggravated) Assistance demanded for executing court process, preventing an offence, suppressing a riot/affray, or apprehending an offender/escapee

punishment_options.condition: Up to one month, or fine up to ₹200, or both
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹500, or both — if assistance is demanded for the specified purposes

sections.key_principle: Duty to assist arises only where the law imposes it (e.g. Cr.P.C. s. 37 on the public to assist Magistrates and police).

sections.heading: Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant
sections.text: Whoever, knowing that, by an order promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, he is directed to abstain from a certain act, or to take certain order with certain property in his possession or under his management, disobeys such direction, shall, if such disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury, or risk of obstruction, annoyance or injury, to any persons lawfully employed, be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both; and if such disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tends to cause a riot or affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: An order promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to do so
Offender knows of the order
Disobeys the direction to abstain from an act or to deal in a certain way with property
Disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury (basic) or danger to life, health or safety, or riot/affray (aggravated)

punishment_options.condition: Up to one month, or fine up to ₹200, or both — obstruction, annoyance or injury
Up to six months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both — danger to human life, health or safety, or riot/affray

sections.key_principle: Basis of prosecutions for violating prohibitory orders (e.g. under Cr.P.C. s. 144, lockdown orders). Intention to cause harm is not required — only knowledge of the order and resulting/likely harm. Cognizance requires a complaint by the public servant (Cr.P.C. s. 195).

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: An order is promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, directing that a religious procession shall not pass down a certain street. A knowingly disobeys the order, and thereby causes danger of riot. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
illustrations.key_principle: Knowingly disobeying a lawful prohibitory order that creates a danger of riot attracts the higher punishment.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: It is not necessary that the offender should intend to produce harm, or contemplate his disobedience as likely to produce harm. It is sufficient that he knows of the order which he disobeys, and that his disobedience produces, or is likely to produce, harm.
explanations.plain_language: Knowledge of the order plus actual or likely harm suffices; intention to harm is not needed.

sections.heading: Threat of injury to public servant
sections.text: Whoever holds out any threat of injury to any public servant, or to any person in whom he believes that public servant to be interested, for the purpose of inducing that public servant to do any act, or to forbear or delay to do any act, connected with the exercise of the public functions of such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Holds out a threat of injury to a public servant or a person in whom he is interested
For the purpose of inducing the public servant to do, forbear or delay any act connected with his public functions
sections.key_principle: Coercion of public servants through threats; 'injury' is defined in s. 44 (body, mind, reputation, property).

sections.heading: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant
sections.text: Whoever holds out any threat of injury to any person for the purpose of inducing that person to refrain or desist from making a legal application for protection against any injury to any public servant legally empowered as such to give such protection, or to cause such protection to be given, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Holds out a threat of injury to any person
To induce that person to refrain or desist from making a legal application for protection against injury
The application is to a public servant legally empowered to give or cause protection
sections.key_principle: Protects access to State protection (e.g. complaints to police or magistrates) from intimidation.

chapters.chapter_title: Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice

chapters_covered: XI — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
key_themes: False evidence — giving, fabricating, using; punishment tiers (ss. 191–200)
Threatening a witness (s. 195A, inserted 2006)
False certificates and declarations (ss. 197–200)
Screening offenders — destroying evidence, false information, harbouring, gifts (ss. 201–203, 212–216A)
Document destruction, false personation, fraudulent decrees and property concealment (ss. 204–210)
False charge (s. 211) — with Chhattisgarh amendment
Public servants and the judicial process — corrupt orders, wrongful commitment, escapes (ss. 217–223, 225A)
Resistance to arrest and rescue (ss. 224–225B)
Conditional remission breach (s. 227); contempt of court proceedings (s. 228)
Victim identity disclosure (s. 228A); juror personation (s. 229); bail-jumping (s. 229A)
notable_amendments: Act 21 of 2000 — 'electronic record' added to ss. 192, 204.
Act 2 of 2006 — s. 195A inserted (w.e.f. 16-4-2006).
Act 3 of 1894, s. 6–8 — Explanations to ss. 203, 212 and s. 216A inserted.
Act 43 of 1983, s. 2 — s. 228A inserted; Act 13 of 2013 and Act 22 of 2018 — offence list amended.
Act 26 of 1955 — 'transportation' replaced by 'imprisonment for life'; s. 226 repealed.
State amendments: Chhattisgarh (s. 211), Arunachal Pradesh (s. 228A).
metadata.case_query: A man files a police complaint alleging that his neighbour raped his niece, knowing the allegation is untrue, in order to get the neighbour jailed over a land dispute; the neighbour is later acquitted. The complainant says that making a complaint cannot be an offence.

sections.heading: Giving false evidence
sections.text: Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence.
ingredients: Legally bound by oath or express provision of law to state the truth, or bound by law to make a declaration
Makes a statement that is false
Knows or believes it false, or does not believe it true

mens_rea_modes.description: Knowledge that the statement is false
Belief that the statement is false
Not believing the statement to be true

sections.key_principle: Definition of perjury-type false evidence. A statement of belief or knowledge that the maker does not hold is false evidence; an honest statement of belief that turns out wrong is not.

illustrations.label: Illustration (a)
illustrations.text: A, in support of a just claim which B has against Z for one thousand rupees, falsely swears on a trial that he heard Z admit the justice of B's claim. A has given false evidence.
illustrations.key_principle: A false oath is false evidence even if it supports a just claim.

illustrations.label: Illustration (b)
illustrations.text: A, being bound by an oath to state the truth, states that he believes a certain signature to be the handwriting of Z, when he does not believe it to be the handwriting of Z. Here A states that which he knows to be false, and therefore gives false evidence.
illustrations.key_principle: Feigned belief is false evidence.

illustrations.label: Illustration (c)
illustrations.text: A, knowing the general character of Z's handwriting, states that he believes a certain signature to be the handwriting of Z; A in good faith believing it to be so. Here A's statement is merely as to his belief, and is true as to his belief, and therefore, although the signature may not be the handwriting of Z, A has not given false evidence.
illustrations.key_principle: An honest statement of belief is not false even if the belief is mistaken.

illustrations.label: Illustration (d)
illustrations.text: A, being bound by an oath to state the truth, states that he knows that Z was at a particular place on a particular day, not knowing anything upon the subject. A gives false evidence whether Z was at that place on the day named or not.
illustrations.key_principle: Claiming knowledge one lacks is false evidence regardless of the truth of the fact.

illustrations.label: Illustration (e)
illustrations.text: A, an interpreter or translator, gives or certifies as a true interpretation or translation of a statement or document which he is bound by oath to interpret or translate truly, that which is not and which he does not believe to be a true interpretation or translation. A has given false evidence.
illustrations.key_principle: A false interpretation or translation on oath is false evidence.

explanations.label: Explanation 1
explanations.text: A statement is within the meaning of this section, whether it is made verbally or otherwise.
explanations.plain_language: Statement may be oral, written or by conduct/signs.

explanations.label: Explanation 2
explanations.text: A false statement as to the belief of the person attesting is within the meaning of this section, and a person may be guilty of giving false evidence by stating that he believes a thing which he does not believe, as well as by stating that he knows a thing which he does not know.
explanations.plain_language: False claims of belief or of knowledge are both false evidence.

sections.heading: Fabricating false evidence
sections.text: Whoever causes any circumstance to exist or makes any false entry in any book or record, or electronic record or makes any document or electronic record containing a false statement, intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding, or in a proceeding taken by law before a public servant as such, or before an arbitrator, and that such circumstance, false entry or false statement, so appearing in evidence, may cause any person who in such proceeding is to form an opinion upon the evidence, to entertain an erroneous opinion touching any point material to the result of such proceeding is said "to fabricate false evidence".
sections.inserted_by: Words relating to electronic records substituted by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and First Sch. (w.e.f. 17-10-2000)
ingredients: Causes a circumstance to exist, or makes a false entry in a book/record/electronic record, or makes a document/electronic record containing a false statement
Intending it to appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding, a proceeding before a public servant or an arbitrator
Intending it to cause an erroneous opinion on a material point
sections.key_principle: Fabrication is the manufacture of false evidence (as opposed to false testimony). Requires intent that it appear in evidence and mislead on a material point.

illustrations.label: Illustration (a)
illustrations.text: A puts jewels into a box belonging to Z, with the intention that they may be found in that box, and that this circumstance may cause Z to be convicted of theft. A has fabricated false evidence.
illustrations.key_principle: Planting evidence to secure a wrongful conviction is fabrication.

illustrations.label: Illustration (b)
illustrations.text: A makes a false entry in his shop-book for the purpose of using it as corroborative evidence in a Court of Justice. A has fabricated false evidence.
illustrations.key_principle: A false book entry meant for use as evidence is fabrication.

illustrations.label: Illustration (c)
illustrations.text: A, with the intention of causing Z to be convicted of a criminal conspiracy, writes a letter in imitation of Z's handwriting, purporting to be addressed to an accomplice in such criminal conspiracy, and puts the letter in a place which he knows that the officers of the police are likely to search. A has fabricated false evidence.
illustrations.key_principle: A forged letter planted for police to find is fabricated evidence.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and the First Sch., for certain words (w.e.f. 17-10-2000).

sections.heading: Punishment for false evidence
sections.text: Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; and whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any other case, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Intentionally gives false evidence in a stage of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates it for use in a judicial proceeding; OR
Intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any other case

punishment_options.condition: Up to seven years and fine — judicial proceeding
Up to three years and fine — any other case

sections.key_principle: Two-tier punishment: seven years for false evidence in judicial proceedings; three years elsewhere. Under Cr.P.C. s. 195(1)(b) the court concerned must file the complaint.

illustrations.label: Illustration (Explanation 2)
illustrations.text: A, in an enquiry before a Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining whether Z ought to be committed for trial, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding, A has given false evidence.
illustrations.verdict: False evidence in a judicial proceeding
illustrations.key_principle: A committal inquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding.

illustrations.label: Illustration (Explanation 3)
illustrations.text: A, in an enquiry before an officer deputed by a Court of Justice to ascertain on the spot the boundaries of land, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding, A has given false evidence.
illustrations.verdict: False evidence in a judicial proceeding
illustrations.key_principle: A court-commissioned local inquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding.

explanations.label: Explanation 1
explanations.text: A trial before a Court-martial is a judicial proceeding.
explanations.plain_language: Court-martial trials count as judicial proceedings.

explanations.label: Explanation 2
explanations.text: An investigation directed by law preliminary to a proceeding before a Court of Justice, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court of Justice.
explanations.plain_language: A statutory pre-trial inquiry is a stage of the judicial proceeding.

explanations.label: Explanation 3
explanations.text: An investigation directed by a Court of Justice according to law, and conducted under the authority of a Court of Justice, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court of Justice.
explanations.plain_language: A court-directed inquiry outside court is also a stage of the proceeding.

footnotes.note_text: The words 'or before a Military Court of Request' rep. by Act 13 of 1889, s. 2 and Sch.

sections.heading: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence
sections.text: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of such false evidence, the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the punishment hereinbefore described.
ingredients: Gives or fabricates false evidence
Intending, or knowing it likely, that a person will be convicted of a capital offence

punishment_options.condition: If an innocent person is convicted and executed in consequence

sections.key_principle: Perjury in capital cases: life or up to 10 years RI; death or the same punishment if an innocent is executed.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1948, for 'by the law of British India or England'.
Subs. by Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., for 'the States'.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment
sections.text: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which by the law for the time being in force in India is not capital, but punishable with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term of seven years or upwards, shall be punished as a person convicted of that offence would be liable to be punished.
ingredients: Gives or fabricates false evidence
Intending, or knowing it likely, to cause conviction of an offence that is not capital but punishable with life imprisonment or imprisonment of seven years or upwards

punishment_options.type: Same punishment as the offence for which conviction was sought

sections.key_principle: Mirror punishment: the false witness is liable to the same punishment as the accused would have suffered.

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A gives false evidence before a Court of Justice, intending thereby to cause Z to be convicted of a dacoity. The punishment of dacoity is imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, with or without fine. A, therefore, is liable to imprisonment for life or imprisonment, with or without fine.
illustrations.verdict: A liable to the punishment for dacoity
illustrations.key_principle: The false witness faces the punishment prescribed for the offence he sought to prove.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by s. 117 and the Schedule, ibid., for 'such transportation' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Threatening any person to give false evidence
sections.text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause that person to give false evidence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both; and if innocent person is convicted and sentenced in consequence of such false evidence, with death or imprisonment for more than seven years, the person who threatens shall be punished with the same punishment and sentence in the same manner and to the same extent such innocent person is punished and sentenced.
ingredients: Threatens another with injury to person, reputation or property (or of one in whom he is interested)
With intent to cause that person to give false evidence

punishment_options.type: Same punishment as the innocent person
punishment_options.condition: If an innocent person is convicted and sentenced to death or imprisonment for more than seven years

sections.key_principle: Witness-intimidation offence. If an innocent person is sentenced to death or more than 7 years' imprisonment because of the false evidence, the threatener suffers the same sentence.

sections.heading: Using evidence known to be false
sections.text: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true or genuine evidence any evidence which he knows to be false or fabricated, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave or fabricated false evidence.
ingredients: Corruptly uses or attempts to use as true or genuine evidence
Evidence known to be false or fabricated

punishment_options.type: Same as for giving or fabricating false evidence

sections.key_principle: Users of known fabricated evidence are punished like the fabricator. 'Corruptly' implies a dishonest intent.

sections.heading: Issuing or signing false certificate
sections.text: Whoever issues or signs any certificate required by law to be given or signed, or relating to any fact of which such certificate is by law admissible in evidence, knowing or believing that such certificate is false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.
ingredients: Issues or signs a certificate required by law or admissible in evidence
Knowing or believing it is false in a material point

punishment_options.type: Same as for giving false evidence

sections.key_principle: False certificates (e.g. medical, birth) are treated as false evidence.

sections.heading: Using as true a certificate known to be false
sections.text: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use any such certificate as a true certificate, knowing the same to be false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.
ingredients: Corruptly uses or attempts to use a certificate (s. 197) as true
Knowing it is false in a material point

punishment_options.type: Same as for giving false evidence

sections.key_principle: Complements s. 197: user of a known false certificate.

sections.heading: False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence
sections.text: Whoever, in any declaration made or subscribed by him, which declaration any Court of Justice, or any public servant or other person, is bound or authorised by law to receive as evidence of any fact, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, touching any point material to the object for which the declaration is made or used, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.
ingredients: Declaration made or subscribed by him, which is by law receivable as evidence
Statement that is false and known/believed false or not believed true
Touching a point material to the declaration's object

punishment_options.type: Same as for giving false evidence

sections.key_principle: Applies to affidavits and statutory declarations that the law lets courts or officials receive as evidence.

sections.heading: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false
sections.text: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true any such declaration, knowing the same to be false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.
ingredients: Corruptly uses or attempts to use a declaration (s. 199) as true
Knowing it is false in a material point

punishment_options.type: Same as for giving false evidence

sections.key_principle: Complements s. 199.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: A declaration which is inadmissible merely upon the ground of some informality, is a declaration within the meaning of sections 199 and 200.
explanations.plain_language: A technical defect in admissibility does not take a declaration outside ss. 199–200.

sections.heading: Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender
sections.text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, causes any evidence of the commission of that offence to disappear, with the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment, or with that intention gives any information respecting the offence which he knows or believes to be false, shall, if the offence which he knows or believes to have been committed is punishable with death be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for any term not extending to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of the imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed
Causes evidence to disappear, or gives false information about the offence
With the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment

punishment_options.condition: Up to seven years and fine — if the offence is punishable with death
Up to three years and fine — if the offence is punishable with life imprisonment or up to ten years

punishment_options.type: Imprisonment of the description provided for the offence
punishment_options.condition: Up to one-fourth of the longest term, or fine, or both — if punishable with less than ten years

sections.key_principle: Screening an offender. The offence must actually have been committed; the three tiers are fixed by the gravity of the screened offence. Commonly charged along with murder (e.g. disposal of a body).

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A, knowing that B has murdered Z, assists B to hide the body with the intention of screening B from punishment. A is liable to imprisonment of either description for seven years, and also to fine.
illustrations.verdict: A liable to up to 7 years and fine
illustrations.key_principle: Helping hide a murder victim's body to protect the killer attracts the top tier.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Intentional omission to give information of offence by person bound to inform
sections.text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, intentionally omits to give any information respecting that offence which he is legally bound to give, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Knowing or having reason to believe an offence has been committed
Legally bound to give information about it
Intentionally omits to give it
sections.key_principle: Applies only where there is a legal duty to inform (e.g. Cr.P.C. s. 39).

sections.heading: Giving false information respecting an offence committed
sections.text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, gives any information respecting that offence which he knows or believes to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Explanation.—In sections 201 and 202 and in this section the word "offence" includes any act committed at any place out of India, which, if committed in India, would be punishable under any of the following sections, namely, 302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460.
sections.inserted_by: Explanation added by Act 3 of 1894, s. 6
ingredients: Knowing or having reason to believe an offence has been committed
Gives information about it which he knows or believes to be false
sections.key_principle: False reporting of an offence (e.g. false FIR content). Unlike s. 182, no intent to misuse the public servant's power is required. Explanation extends 'offence' to listed offences committed abroad.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: In sections 201 and 202 and in this section the word "offence" includes any act committed at any place out of India, which, if committed in India, would be punishable under any of the following sections, namely, 302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460.
explanations.plain_language: Listed serious offences committed abroad count as 'offences' for ss. 201–203.

footnotes.note_text: Added by Act 3 of 1894, s. 6.
The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.

sections.heading: Destruction of document to prevent its production as evidence
sections.text: Whoever secretes or destroys any document or electronic record which he may be lawfully compelled to produce as evidence in a Court of Justice, or in any proceeding lawfully held before a public servant, as such, or obliterates or renders illegible the whole or any part of such document or electronic record with the intention of preventing the same from being produced or used as evidence before such Court or public servant as aforesaid, or after he shall have been lawfully summoned or required to produce the same for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Secretes or destroys a document/electronic record, or obliterates/renders illegible any part
Which he may be lawfully compelled to produce as evidence
With the intention of preventing its production or use as evidence
sections.key_principle: Destruction/concealment of documentary evidence. Covers electronic records since 2000.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 21 of 2000, s. 91 and the First Sch., for 'document' (w.e.f. 17-10-2000).

sections.heading: False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution
sections.text: Whoever falsely personates another, and in such assumed character makes any admission or statement, or confesses judgment, or causes any process to be issued or becomes bail or security, or does any other act in any suit or criminal prosecution, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Falsely personates another
In that character makes an admission/statement, confesses judgment, causes process to issue, becomes bail/security, or does any other act in a suit or criminal prosecution
sections.key_principle: Impersonation in litigation, e.g. standing as surety under a false identity.

sections.heading: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
sections.text: Whoever fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers or delivers to any person any property or any interest therein, intending thereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in satisfaction of a fine, under a sentence which has been pronounced, or which he knows to be likely to be pronounced, by a Court of Justice or other competent authority, or from being taken in execution of a decree or order which has been made, or which he knows to be likely to be made by a Court of Justice in a civil suit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers or delivers property or an interest in it
Intending to prevent its seizure as a forfeiture, in satisfaction of a fine, or in execution of a decree or order (made or likely to be made)
sections.key_principle: Asset-hiding to defeat fines, forfeitures or decrees — including anticipatory transfers where the sentence or decree is likely.

sections.heading: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
sections.text: Whoever fraudulently accepts, receives or claims any property or any interest therein, knowing that he has no right or rightful claim to such property or interest, or practices any deception touching any right to any property or any interest therein, intending thereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in satisfaction of a fine, under a sentence which has been pronounced, or which he knows to be likely to be pronounced by a Court of Justice or other competent authority, or from being taken in execution of a decree or order which has been made, or which he knows to be likely to be made by a Court of Justice in a civil suit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently accepts/receives/claims property knowing he has no right, or practises deception about a right to property
Intending to prevent its seizure as a forfeiture, in satisfaction of a fine, or in execution of a decree or order
sections.key_principle: The 'benami claimant' counterpart of s. 206.

sections.heading: Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due
sections.text: Whoever fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against him at the suit of any person for a sum not due or for a larger sum than is due to such person or for any property or interest in property to which such person is not entitled, or fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be executed against him after it has been satisfied, or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently causes or suffers a decree/order against himself for a sum not due, a larger sum than due, or property the decree-holder is not entitled to; OR
Fraudulently causes or suffers a decree to be executed after satisfaction
sections.key_principle: Collusive decrees by the judgment-debtor to defeat creditors.

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A institutes a suit against Z. Z, knowing that A is likely to obtain a decree against him, fraudulently suffers a judgment to pass against him for a larger amount at the suit of B, who has no just claim against him, in order that B, either on his own account or for the benefit of Z, may share in the proceeds of any sale of Z's property which may be made under A's decree. Z has committed an offence under this section.
illustrations.key_principle: A collusive decree to dilute a genuine creditor's recovery is an offence.

sections.heading: Dishonestly making false claim in Court
sections.text: Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly, or with intent to injure or annoy any person, makes in a Court of Justice any claim which he knows to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Makes a claim in a Court of Justice
Knows the claim is false
Fraudulently or dishonestly, or with intent to injure or annoy any person
sections.key_principle: Knowingly false civil claims.

sections.heading: Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due
sections.text: Whoever fraudulently obtains a decree or order against any person for a sum not due, or for a larger sum than is due or for any property or interest in property to which he is not entitled, or fraudulently causes a decree or order to be executed against any person after it has been satisfied or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, or fraudulently suffers or permits any such act to be done in his name, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently obtains a decree/order for a sum not due, a larger sum, or property not owed
OR fraudulently causes execution after satisfaction
OR fraudulently suffers or permits such an act in his name
sections.key_principle: Decree-holder side counterpart of s. 208.

sections.heading: False charge of offence made with intent to injure
sections.text: Whoever, with intent to cause injury to any person, institutes or causes to be instituted any criminal proceeding against that person, or falsely charges any person with having committed an offence, knowing that there is no just or lawful ground for such proceeding or charge against that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and if such criminal proceeding be instituted on a false charge of an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for seven years or upwards, shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Institutes or causes to be instituted a criminal proceeding, or falsely charges a person with an offence
With intent to cause injury
Knowing there is no just or lawful ground

punishment_options.condition: Up to two years, or fine, or both
Up to seven years and fine — if the false charge is of an offence punishable with death, life imprisonment or imprisonment of seven years or upwards

sections.key_principle: Malicious prosecution / false complaint offence. Courts typically require an acquittal or finding of falsity first, and a complaint under Cr.P.C. s. 195(1)(b).

state_amendments.text: In section 211, the following proviso is inserted: Provided that, if such criminal proceeding be instituted on a false charge of an offence punishable under section 354, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 354E, 376B, 376C, 376F, 509, 509A or 509B, it shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Harbouring offender
sections.text: Whenever an offence has been committed, whoever harbours or conceals a person whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the offender, with the intention of screening him from legal punishment, shall, if the offence is punishable with death, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year, and not to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.
sections.inserted_by: Explanation inserted by Act 3 of 1894, s. 7
ingredients: An offence has been committed
Harbours or conceals a person he knows or has reason to believe to be the offender
With the intention of screening him from legal punishment

punishment_options.condition: Up to five years and fine — if the offence is punishable with death
Up to three years and fine — if punishable with life imprisonment or up to ten years

punishment_options.type: Imprisonment of the description provided for the offence
punishment_options.condition: Up to one-fourth of the longest term, or fine, or both — if punishable with imprisonment of one to ten years

sections.key_principle: Harbouring is defined in s. 52A. Spouses of the offender are exempt. 'Offence' includes listed offences committed outside India.

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A, knowing that B has committed dacoity, knowingly conceals B in order to screen him from legal punishment. Here, as B is liable to imprisonment for life, A is liable to imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding three years, and is also liable to fine.
illustrations.verdict: A liable to up to 3 years and fine
illustrations.key_principle: Concealing a dacoit attracts the middle tier.

explanations.label: Explanation (as printed)
explanations.text: "Offence" in this section includes any act committed at any place out of India, which, if committed in India, would be punishable under any of the following sections, namely, 302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460; and every such act shall, for the purposes of this section, be deemed to be punishable as if the accused person had been guilty of it in India.
explanations.plain_language: Listed serious offences committed abroad are treated as offences committed in India for this section.

exceptions: This provision shall not extend to any case in which the harbour or concealment is by the husband or wife of the offender.

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 3 of 1894, s. 7.
The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951 s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment
sections.text: Whoever accepts or attempts to obtain, or agrees to accept, any gratification for himself or any other person, or any restitution of property to himself or any other person, in consideration of his concealing an offence or of his screening any person from legal punishment for any offence, or of his not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment, shall, if the offence is punishable with death, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment not extending to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Accepts, attempts to obtain, or agrees to accept a gratification or restitution of property
In consideration of concealing an offence, screening a person from punishment, or not proceeding against a person

punishment_options.condition: Up to seven years and fine — capital offence
Up to three years and fine — life imprisonment or up to ten years

punishment_options.type: Imprisonment of the description provided for the offence
punishment_options.condition: Up to one-fourth of the longest term, or fine, or both — imprisonment less than ten years

sections.key_principle: Taking a bribe to hush up an offence. Not applicable where the offence may lawfully be compounded (see Exception below s. 214).

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender
sections.text: Whoever gives or causes, or offers or agrees to give or cause, any gratification to any person, or restores or causes the restoration of any property to any person, in consideration of that person's concealing an offence, or of his screening any person from legal punishment for any offence, or of his not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment, shall, if the offence is punishable with death, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment not extending to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Gives, causes, offers or agrees to give a gratification, or restores/causes restoration of property
In consideration of concealing an offence, screening a person or not proceeding against a person

punishment_options.condition: Up to seven years and fine — capital offence
Up to three years and fine — life imprisonment or up to ten years

punishment_options.type: Imprisonment of the description provided for the offence
punishment_options.condition: Up to one-fourth of the longest term, or fine, or both — imprisonment less than ten years

sections.key_principle: The giver's counterpart to s. 213.
exceptions: The provisions of sections 213 and 214 do not extend to any case in which the offence may lawfully be compounded.
sections.amendment_note: Exception substituted by Act 8 of 1882, s. 6 for the original exception; illustrations repealed by Act 10 of 1882.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 42 of 1953, s. 4 and the Third Sch., for 'to restore or cause the restoration of'.

sections.heading: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.
sections.text: Whoever takes or agrees or consents to take any gratification under pretence or on account of helping any person to recover any movable property of which he shall have been deprived by any offence punishable under this Code, shall, unless he uses all means in his power to cause the offender to be apprehended and convicted of the offence, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Takes, or agrees or consents to take, a gratification
Under pretence or on account of helping a person recover movable property lost through an offence
Does not use all means to cause the offender to be apprehended and convicted
sections.key_principle: Prevents 'recovery agents' from taking rewards while allowing the offender to escape.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 8 of 1882, s. 6, for the original exception.
Illustrations rep. by Act 10 of 1882, s. 2 and the First Sch.

sections.heading: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered
sections.text: Whenever any person convicted of or charged with an offence, being in lawful custody for that offence, escapes from such custody, or whenever a public servant, in the exercise of the lawful powers of such public servant, orders a certain person to be apprehended for an offence, whoever, knowing of such escape or order for apprehension, harbours or conceals that person with the intention of preventing him from being apprehended, shall be punished in the manner following, that is to say, if the offence for which the person was in custody or is ordered to be apprehended is punishable with death, he shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years, he shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with or without fine; and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year and not to ten years, he shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of the imprisonment provided for such offence, or with fine, or with both.
sections.inserted_by: Explanation inserted by Act 10 of 1886, s. 23
ingredients: A convicted/charged person in lawful custody escapes, or a public servant orders apprehension
Offender knows of the escape or order
Harbours or conceals the person with intent to prevent apprehension

punishment_options.condition: Up to seven years and fine — capital offence
Up to three years, with or without fine — life imprisonment or ten years

punishment_options.type: Imprisonment of the description provided for the offence
punishment_options.condition: Up to one-fourth of the longest term, or fine, or both — one to ten years

sections.key_principle: Harbouring an escapee or a person wanted under an arrest order. Spouse exempt. 'Offence' includes extraditable foreign acts.

explanations.label: Explanation (as printed)
explanations.text: "Offence" in this section includes also any act or omission of which a person is alleged to have been guilty out of India, which, if he had been guilty of it in India, would have been punishable as an offence, and for which he is, under any law relating to extradition, or otherwise, liable to be apprehended or detained in custody in India, and every such act or omission shall, for the purposes of this section, be deemed to be punishable as if the accused person had been guilty of it in India.
explanations.plain_language: Acts abroad that would be offences in India and make the person extraditable are covered.

exceptions: The provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour or concealment is by the husband or wife of the person to be apprehended.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).
Ins. by Act 10 of 1886, s. 23.
The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.
The words 'or under the Fugitive Offenders Act, 1881,' omitted by Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch.

sections.heading: Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits
sections.text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that any persons are about to commit or have recently committed robbery or dacoity, harbours them or any of them, with the intention of facilitating the commission of such robbery or dacoity, or of screening them or any of them from punishment, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Knowing or having reason to believe persons are about to commit or have recently committed robbery or dacoity
Harbours them
With intention to facilitate the offence or screen them from punishment
sections.key_principle: Special harbouring provision for robbers and dacoits — mandatory rigorous imprisonment. Spouse exempt; place of offence (in or out of India) is immaterial.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: For the purposes of this section it is immaterial whether the robbery or dacoity is intended to be committed, or has been committed, within or without India.
explanations.plain_language: Location of the robbery/dacoity is irrelevant.

exceptions: This provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour is by the husband or wife of the offender.

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 3 of 1894, s. 8.

sections.heading: Definition of "harbour" in sections 212, 216 and 216A
sections.text: [Definition of "harbour" in sections 212, 216 and 216A.] Rep. by the Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1942 (8 of 1942), s. 3.
sections.repealed_by: Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1942 (8 of 1942), s. 3 (see now s. 52A)
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1942 (8 of 1942), s. 3 (see now s. 52A)
