sections.heading: Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant, intending thereby to save, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby save, any person from legal punishment, or subject him to a less punishment than that to which he is liable, or with intent to save, or knowing that he is likely thereby to save, any property from forfeiture or any charge to which it is liable by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
Knowingly disobeys a direction of law as to his conduct
Intending (or knowing it likely) to save a person from punishment or subject him to lesser punishment, or to save property from forfeiture
sections.key_principle: Public servant bending the law to shield an accused or property — compare s. 166 (intent to injure).

sections.heading: Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the preparation of any record or other writing, frames that record or writing in a manner which he knows to be incorrect, with intent to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, loss or injury to the public or to any person, or with intent thereby to save, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby save, any person from legal punishment, or with intent to save, or knowing that he is likely thereby to save, any property from forfeiture or other charge to which it is liable by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant charged with preparing a record or writing
Frames it in a manner he knows to be incorrect
Intending (or knowing it likely) to cause loss/injury to the public or a person, or to save a person from punishment or property from forfeiture
sections.key_principle: Falsification of official records (e.g. police case diaries, panchnamas) by public servants.

sections.heading: Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, corruptly or maliciously makes or pronounces in any stage of a judicial proceeding, any report, order, verdict, or decision which he knows to be contrary to law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant
Makes or pronounces in a stage of a judicial proceeding a report, order, verdict or decision
Knows it to be contrary to law
Acts corruptly or maliciously
sections.key_principle: Corrupt or malicious perversion of judicial process. Mere error of law is not enough — knowledge plus corrupt/malicious motive is required.

sections.heading: Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law
sections.text: Whoever, being in any office which gives him legal authority to commit persons for trial or to confinement, or to keep persons in confinement, corruptly or maliciously commits any person for trial or to confinement, or keeps any person in confinement, in the exercise of that authority knowing that in so doing he is acting contrary to law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Holds an office giving legal authority to commit for trial/confinement or keep persons in confinement
Corruptly or maliciously commits or keeps a person in confinement
Knowing he is acting contrary to law
sections.key_principle: Wrongful commitment by an authorised officer (e.g. magistrate, jailer) with knowledge of illegality and corrupt/malicious motive.

sections.heading: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, legally bound as such public servant to apprehend or to keep in confinement any person charged with or liable to be apprehended for an offence, intentionally omits to apprehend such person, or intentionally suffers such person to escape, or intentionally aids such person in escaping or attempting to escape from such confinement, shall be punished as follows, that is to say:— with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, with or without fine, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended, was charged with, or liable to be apprehended for, an offence punishable with death; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with or without fine, if the person ... was charged with, or liable to be apprehended for, an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, with or without fine, if the person ... was charged with, or liable to be apprehended for, an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term less than ten years.
ingredients: Offender is a public servant legally bound to apprehend or confine a person charged with/liable to be apprehended for an offence
Intentionally omits to apprehend, intentionally suffers escape, or intentionally aids escape or attempt to escape

punishment_options.condition: Up to seven years, with or without fine — capital offence
Up to three years, with or without fine — life imprisonment or up to ten years
Up to two years, with or without fine — imprisonment less than ten years

sections.key_principle: Intentional dereliction by a public servant; tiered by gravity of the offence charged. Negligent escape is dealt with in s. 223/225A.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant, legally bound as such public servant to apprehend or to keep in confinement any person under sentence of a Court of Justice for any offence or lawfully committed to custody, intentionally omits to apprehend such person, or intentionally suffers such person to escape or intentionally aids such person in escaping or attempting to escape from such confinement, shall be punished as follows, that is to say:— with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, with or without fine, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended, is under sentence of death; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, with or without fine, if the person ... is subject, by a sentence of a Court of Justice, or by virtue of a commutation of such sentence, to imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term of ten years, or upwards; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, if the person ... is subject by a sentence of a Court of Justice, to imprisonment for a term not extending to ten years or if the person was lawfully committed to custody.
ingredients: Public servant legally bound to apprehend or confine a person under sentence of a court or lawfully committed to custody
Intentionally omits to apprehend, suffers escape or aids escape/attempt

punishment_options.condition: Or imprisonment up to fourteen years, with or without fine — person under sentence of death
Up to seven years, with or without fine — person sentenced to life or ten years or more
Up to three years, or fine, or both — person sentenced to less than ten years or lawfully committed to custody

sections.key_principle: Counterpart of s. 221 for convicts and persons lawfully committed to custody.
sections.amendment_note: 'or lawfully committed to custody' inserted by Act 27 of 1870, s. 8.

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 27 of 1870, s. 8.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to keep in confinement any person charged with or convicted of any offence or lawfully committed to custody, negligently suffers such person to escape from confinement, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Public servant legally bound to keep a person in confinement
Person is charged with/convicted of an offence or lawfully committed to custody
Negligently suffers the person to escape
sections.key_principle: Negligence (not intention) in guarding prisoners — milder than ss. 221–222; compare s. 129 for State prisoners.

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 27 of 1870, s. 8.

sections.heading: Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension
sections.text: Whoever intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction to the lawful apprehension of himself for any offence with which he is charged or of which he has been convicted, or escapes or attempts to escape from any custody in which he is lawfully detained for any such offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Intentionally offers resistance or illegal obstruction to lawful apprehension of himself; OR
Escapes or attempts to escape from lawful custody
For an offence charged or of which convicted
sections.key_principle: Self-resistance to lawful arrest. The punishment is additional to that for the underlying offence.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: The punishment in this section is in addition to the punishment for which the person to be apprehended or detained in custody was liable for the offence with which he was charged, or of which he was convicted.
explanations.plain_language: The s. 224 punishment is cumulative with the punishment for the original offence.

sections.heading: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person
sections.text: Whoever intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction to the lawful apprehension of any other person for an offence, or rescues or attempts to rescue any other person from any custody in which that person is lawfully detained for an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; or, if the person to be apprehended, or the person rescued or attempted to be rescued, is charged with or liable to be apprehended for an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; or, if ... punishable with death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; or, if ... is liable under the sentence of a Court of Justice, or by virtue of a commutation of such a sentence, to imprisonment for life or imprisonment, for a term of ten years, or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; or, if ... is under sentence of death, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Intentionally offers resistance or illegal obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person; OR
Rescues or attempts to rescue another from lawful custody
For an offence

punishment_options.condition: Up to two years, or fine, or both — basic
Up to three years and fine — person charged with life imprisonment or ten-year offence
Up to seven years and fine — person charged with a capital offence
Up to seven years and fine — person sentenced to life or ten years or more
Or imprisonment up to ten years and fine — person under sentence of death

sections.key_principle: Five-tier rescue/obstruction offence based on the gravity of the offence or sentence of the person rescued.

footnotes.note_text: The words 'or to' omitted by Act 36 of 1957, s. 3 and the Second Sch.
The word 'transportation' omitted by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch. (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).
The words 'or penal servitude' omitted by Act 17 of 1949, s. 2 (w.e.f. 6-4-1949).

sections.heading: Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for
sections.text: Whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to apprehend, or to keep in confinement, any person in any case not provided for in section 221, section 222 or section 223, or in any other law for the time being in force, omits to apprehend that person or suffers him to escape from confinement, shall be punished— (a) if he does so intentionally, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine or with both; and (b) if he does so negligently, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.inserted_by: Substituted by Act 10 of 1886, s. 24(1) (original s. 225A inserted by Act 27 of 1870, s. 9)
ingredients: Public servant legally bound to apprehend or confine a person
Case not covered by ss. 221–223 or other law
Omits to apprehend or suffers escape (intentionally or negligently)

punishment_options.condition: Up to three years, or fine, or both — intentional
Up to two years, or fine, or both — negligent

sections.key_principle: Residuary provision for omissions to apprehend / escapes not provided for elsewhere.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 10 of 1886, s. 24(1), for section 225A which had been ins. by Act 27 of 1870, s. 9.

sections.heading: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue in cases not otherwise provided for
sections.text: Whoever, in any case not provided for in section 224 or section 225 or in any other law for the time being in force, intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction to the lawful apprehension of himself or of any other person, or escapes or attempts to escape from any custody in which he is lawfully detained, or rescues or attempts to rescue any other person from any custody in which that person is lawfully detained, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Case not provided for in ss. 224, 225 or other law
Intentionally resists or obstructs lawful apprehension of himself or another; OR escapes/attempts to escape from lawful custody; OR rescues/attempts to rescue another
sections.key_principle: Residuary provision for resistance, escape and rescue (e.g. civil arrests).

sections.heading: Unlawful return from transportation
sections.text: [Unlawful return from transportation.] Rep. by the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1955 (26 of 1955), s. 117 and the Sch (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).
sections.repealed_by: Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1955 (26 of 1955), s. 117 and the Sch (w.e.f. 1-1-1956)
sections.key_principle: Repealed — Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1955 (26 of 1955), s. 117 and the Sch (w.e.f. 1-1-1956)

sections.heading: Violation of condition of remission of punishment
sections.text: Whoever, having accepted any conditional remission of punishment, knowingly violates any condition on which such remission was granted, shall be punished with the punishment to which he was originally sentenced, if he has already suffered no part of that punishment, and if he has suffered any part of that punishment, then with so much of that punishment as he has not already suffered.
ingredients: Has accepted a conditional remission of punishment
Knowingly violates a condition of the remission

punishment_options.condition: If he has suffered no part of it

punishment_options.type: Unexpired portion of the original sentence
punishment_options.condition: If he has already suffered part of it

sections.key_principle: Revival of the remitted sentence on breach of conditions; knowledge of the condition is essential.

sections.heading: Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding
sections.text: Whoever intentionally offers any insult, or causes any interruption to any public servant, while such public servant is sitting in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Intentionally offers an insult or causes an interruption
To a public servant while sitting in any stage of a judicial proceeding
sections.key_principle: Protects dignity and order of judicial proceedings; intention is essential (accidental interruption is not covered).

sections.heading: Disclosure of identity of the victim of certain offences, etc.
sections.text: (1) Whoever prints or publishes the name or any matter which may make known the identity of any person against whom an offence under section 376, section 376A, section 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB or section 376E is alleged or found to have been committed (hereafter in this section referred to as the victim) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine. (2) Nothing in sub-section (1) extends to any printing or publication of the name or any matter which may make known the identity of the victim if such printing or publication is— (a) by or under the order in writing of the officer-in-charge of the police station or the police officer making the investigation into such offence acting in good faith for the purposes of such investigation; or (b) by, or with the authorisation in writing of, the victim; or (c) where the victim is dead or minor or of unsound mind, by, or with the authorisation in writing of, the next of kin of the victim: Provided that no such authorisation shall be given by the next of kin to anybody other than the chairman or the secretary, by whatever name called, of any recognised welfare institution or organisation. (3) Whoever prints or publishes any matter in relation to any proceeding before a court with respect to an offence referred to in sub-section (1) without the previous permission of such court shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: (1) Prints or publishes the victim's name or any matter that may reveal identity, where the offence alleged or found is under s. 376, 376A, 376AB, 376B, 376C, 376D, 376DA, 376DB or 376E
(3) Prints or publishes court-proceeding matter relating to such offence without the court's previous permission

punishment_options.condition: Up to two years and fine — sub-section (1)
Up to two years and fine — sub-section (3)

sections.key_principle: Protects the privacy and dignity of rape/sexual-offence victims. Exceptions for investigation and welfare-institution authorisation. Publication of High Court and Supreme Court judgments is not an offence under sub-section (3).

subsections.heading: Disclosure of victim's identity
subsections.punishment: Imprisonment up to two years and fine

subsections.heading: Exceptions
subsections.text: (a) By/under written order of the police station in-charge or investigating officer acting in good faith for investigation; (b) by or with written authorisation of the victim; (c) where the victim is dead, minor or of unsound mind, by or with written authorisation of the next of kin — which must be given only to the chairman/secretary of a recognised welfare institution or organisation.
subsections.explanation: 'Recognised welfare institution or organisation' means a social welfare institution recognised by the Central or State Government.

subsections.heading: Publication of court-proceeding matter without permission
subsections.punishment: Imprisonment up to two years and fine
subsections.explanation: Printing or publication of a judgment of a High Court or the Supreme Court is not an offence.

state_amendments.text: In section 228A(1), for 'offence under section 376, section 376A, section 376B, section 376C or section 376D or section 376E' substitute 'offence under section 376, section 376A, section 376AA, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA or section 376E'.

sections.amendment_note: Offence list amended by Act 13 of 2013, s. 4 (w.e.f. 3-2-2013) and Act 22 of 2018, s. 3 (w.e.f. 21-4-2018).

footnotes.note_text: Ins. by Act 43 of 1983, s. 2.
Subs. by Act 13 of 2013, s. 4, for 'offence under section 376, section 376A, section 376B, section 376C or section 376D' (w.e.f. 3-2-2013).
Subs. by Act 22 of 2018, s. 3, for 'section 376A, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D' (w.e.f. 21-4-2018).

sections.heading: Personation of a juror or assessor
sections.text: Whoever, by personation or otherwise, shall intentionally cause, or knowingly suffer himself to be returned, empanelled or sworn as a juryman or assessor in any case in which he knows that he is not entitled by law to be so returned, empanelled or sworn, or knowing himself to have been so returned, empanelled or sworn contrary to law, shall voluntarily serve on such jury or as such assessor, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Intentionally causes, or knowingly suffers himself to be, returned/empanelled/sworn as juror or assessor
Knows he is not entitled by law; OR knowing the return was contrary to law, voluntarily serves
sections.key_principle: Protects the integrity of juries and assessors.

sections.heading: Failure by person released on bail or bond to appear in court
sections.text: Whoever, having been charged with an offence and released on bail or on bond without sureties, fails without sufficient cause (the burden of proving which shall lie upon him), to appear in court in accordance with the terms of the bail or bond, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Charged with an offence and released on bail or on bond without sureties
Fails to appear in court per the terms of bail/bond
Without sufficient cause — burden of proof on the accused
sections.key_principle: Bail-jumping offence with a reverse burden of proof — the accused must prove sufficient cause for non-appearance. Punishment is additional to that for the original offence and to forfeiture of the bond.
sections.reverse_burden_note: The accused must prove sufficient cause for failing to appear.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: The punishment under this section is— (a) in addition to the punishment to which the offender would be liable on a conviction for the offence with which he has been charged; and (b) without prejudice to the power of the court to order forfeiture of the bond.
explanations.plain_language: Cumulative with the original offence's punishment and with bond forfeiture.

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps

chapters_covered: XII — Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps
key_themes: Definition of coin and Indian coin (s. 230)
Counterfeiting coin and Indian coin; instruments and possession (ss. 231–235)
Import/export and abetment abroad (ss. 236–238)
Uttering counterfeit coin — knowing at the outset (ss. 239–240, 242–243) vs learning later (s. 241)
Mint employee offences (ss. 244–245)
Altering weight, composition or appearance of coin and dealing in altered coin (ss. 246–254)
Government revenue stamps — counterfeiting, trade, use and reuse (ss. 255–263)
Fictitious postage stamps — fine and forfeiture (s. 263A)
notable_amendments: A.O. 1950 — 'Queen's coin' replaced by 'Indian coin'.
Act 26 of 1955 — 'transportation for life' replaced by 'imprisonment for life' in ss. 232, 238, 255.
Act 3 of 1895 — s. 263A added; Act 6 of 1896 — illustration (e) to s. 230 added; Act 19 of 1872 — first paragraph of s. 230 substituted.
metadata.case_query: A shopkeeper receives a forged ₹500 note-like coin set from a customer without noticing, discovers it was counterfeit the next day, and passes it on to another customer as genuine, saying he lost money on it.

sections.heading: "Coin" defined
sections.text: Coin is metal used for the time being as money, and stamped and issued by the authority of some State or Sovereign Power in order to be so used. Indian coin.—Indian coin is metal stamped and issued by the authority of the Government of India in order to be used as money; and metal which has been so stamped and issued shall continue to be Indian coin for the purposes of this Chapter, notwithstanding that it may have ceased to be used as money.
ingredients: Coin: metal used as money for the time being, stamped and issued by a State or Sovereign Power
Indian coin: metal stamped and issued by the Government of India to be used as money — remains Indian coin even after ceasing to be money
sections.key_principle: Definition of coin for Chapter XII. Medals, cowries and unstamped copper are not coin; demonetised Indian coin continues to be 'Indian coin'.

illustrations.label: Illustration (a)
illustrations.text: Cowries are not coin.
illustrations.key_principle: Cowries are not stamped and issued as money by a State.

illustrations.label: Illustration (b)
illustrations.text: Lumps of unstamped copper, though used as money, are not coin.
illustrations.key_principle: Stamping and issue by authority are essential.

illustrations.label: Illustration (c)
illustrations.text: Medals are not coin, inasmuch as they are not intended to be used as money.
illustrations.key_principle: Medals are not intended to be money.

illustrations.label: Illustration (d)
illustrations.text: The coin denominated as the Company's rupee is Indian coin.
illustrations.key_principle: Historic coin issued by the Company's authority is Indian coin.

illustrations.label: Illustration (e)
illustrations.text: The "Farukhabad rupee", which was formerly used as money under the authority of the Government of India, is Indian coin although it is no longer so used.
illustrations.key_principle: Demonetised coin remains Indian coin.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 19 of 1872, s. 1, for the first paragraph.
Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for the second paragraph.
Subs. ibid., for 'the Queen's coin'.
Added by Act 6 of 1896, s. 1(2).
Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen's coin'.

sections.heading: Counterfeiting coin
sections.text: Whoever counterfeits or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Counterfeits coin, or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting
sections.key_principle: Counterfeiting general coin (not Indian coin). A person who makes a genuine coin appear to be a different coin also counterfeits.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: A person commits this offence who intending to practise deception, or knowing it to be likely that deception will thereby be practised, causes a genuine coin to appear like a different coin.
explanations.plain_language: Making a genuine coin look like a different (more valuable) coin is counterfeiting.

sections.heading: Counterfeiting Indian coin
sections.text: Whoever counterfeits, or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting Indian coin, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Counterfeits, or knowingly performs part of the process of counterfeiting, Indian coin
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 231 for Indian coin.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'the Queen's coin'.
Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting coin
sections.text: Whoever makes or mends, or performs any part of the process of making or mending, or buys, sells or disposes of, any die or instrument, for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Makes, mends, buys, sells or disposes of a die or instrument
For use in counterfeiting coin, or knowing/having reason to believe so
sections.key_principle: Preparation offence — tools for counterfeiting coin.

sections.heading: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Indian coin
sections.text: Whoever makes or mends, or performs any part of the process of making or mending or buys, sells or disposes of, any die or instrument, for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting Indian coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Makes, mends, buys, sells or disposes of a die or instrument
For use in counterfeiting Indian coin, or knowing/having reason to believe so
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 233 for Indian coin.

sections.heading: Possession of instrument or material for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin
sections.text: Whoever is in possession of any instrument or material, for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin, or knowing or having reason to believe that the same is intended to be used for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if the coin to be counterfeited is Indian coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Possession of an instrument or material
For counterfeiting coin, or knowing/having reason to believe it is intended for that purpose

punishment_options.condition: Up to three years and fine — coin
Up to ten years and fine — if Indian coin

sections.key_principle: Possession-based preparation offence with two tiers.

sections.heading: Abetting in India the counterfeiting out of India of coin
sections.text: Whoever, being within India abets the counterfeiting of coin out of India shall be punished in the same manner as if he abetted the counterfeiting of such coin within India.
ingredients: Being within India
Abets counterfeiting of coin outside India

punishment_options.type: Same as for abetting counterfeiting within India

sections.key_principle: Extra-territorial abetment (cf. s. 108A) in the coin context.

footnotes.note_text: The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.

sections.heading: Import or export of counterfeit coin
sections.text: Whoever imports into India, or exports therefrom, any counterfeit coin, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Imports into or exports from India counterfeit coin
Knowing or having reason to believe it is counterfeit
sections.key_principle: Cross-border movement of counterfeit coin.

sections.heading: Import or export of counterfeits of the Indian coin
sections.text: Whoever imports into India, or exports therefrom, any counterfeit coin, which he knows or has reason to believe to be a counterfeit of Indian coin, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Imports or exports counterfeit coin
Knowing or having reason to believe it is a counterfeit of Indian coin
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 237 for Indian coin.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'Queen's coin'.

sections.heading: Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit
sections.text: Whoever, having any counterfeit coin, which at the time when he became possessed of it, he knew to be counterfeit, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers the same to any persons or attempts to induce any person to receive it, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Possesses counterfeit coin, knowing it to be counterfeit when he became possessed
Fraudulently or with intent that fraud be committed, delivers it or attempts to induce another to receive it
sections.key_principle: 'Uttering' counterfeit coin with guilty knowledge from the start.

sections.heading: Delivery of Indian coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit
sections.text: Whoever, having any counterfeit coin which is a counterfeit of Indian coin, and which, at the time when he became possessed of it, he knew to be a counterfeit of Indian coin, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers the same to any person, or attempts to induce any person to receive it, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Possesses counterfeit Indian coin, knowing it to be counterfeit when he became possessed
Fraudulently delivers it or attempts to induce another to receive it
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 239 for Indian coin.

sections.heading: Delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit
sections.text: Whoever delivers to any other person as genuine, or attempts to induce any other person to receive as genuine, any counterfeit coin which he knows to be counterfeit, but which he did not know to be counterfeit at the time when he took it into his possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine to an amount which may extend to ten times the value of the coin counterfeited, or with both.
ingredients: Delivers (or attempts to induce another to receive) counterfeit coin as genuine
Knows it is counterfeit now, but did not know when he took possession

punishment_options.condition: Up to ten times the value of the coin counterfeited

sections.key_principle: Innocent receiver who later passes on the coin knowingly — a milder offence.

illustrations.label: Illustration
illustrations.text: A, a coiner, delivers counterfeit Company's rupees to his accomplice B, for the purpose of uttering them. B sells the rupees to C, another utterer, who buys them knowing them to be counterfeit. C pays away the rupees for goods to D, who receives them, not knowing them to be counterfeit. D, after receiving the rupees, discovers that they are counterfeit and pays them away as if they were good. Here D is punishable only under this section, but B and C are punishable under section 239 or 240, as the case may be.
illustrations.verdict: D punishable under s. 241; B and C under s. 239/240
illustrations.key_principle: Only the person who learned of the counterfeit after taking possession falls under s. 241.

sections.heading: Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of counterfeit coin, having known at the time when he became possessed thereof that such coin was counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Fraudulently or with intent that fraud be committed, in possession of counterfeit coin
Knew it was counterfeit when he became possessed of it
sections.key_principle: Mere guilty possession with fraudulent intent.

sections.heading: Possession of Indian coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of counterfeit coin, which is a counterfeit of Indian coin, having known at the time when he became possessed of it that it was counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Fraudulently in possession of counterfeit Indian coin
Knew it was counterfeit when he became possessed of it
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 242.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'the Queen's coin'.

sections.heading: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law
sections.text: Whoever, being employed in any mint lawfully established in India, does any act, or omits what he is legally bound to do, with the intention of causing any coin issued from that mint to be of a different weight or composition from the weight or composition fixed by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Employed in a lawfully established mint in India
Does an act or omits a legal duty
With intention of causing coin to differ in weight or composition from that fixed by law
sections.key_principle: Insider offence by mint employees.

footnotes.note_text: The words 'British India' have successively been subs. by the A.O. 1948, the A.O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.

sections.heading: Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint
sections.text: Whoever, without lawful authority, takes out of any mint, lawfully established in India, any coining tool or instrument, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Without lawful authority takes a coining tool or instrument out of a lawful mint in India
sections.key_principle: Theft of coining instruments from a mint.

sections.heading: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of coin
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly performs on any coin any operation which diminishes the weight or alters the composition of that coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Fraudulently or dishonestly performs an operation on coin
Which diminishes its weight or alters its composition
sections.key_principle: 'Sweating'/'clipping' of coin.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: A person who scoops out part of the coin and puts anything else into the cavity alters the composition of the coin.
explanations.plain_language: Hollowing out a coin and filling it with other material alters its composition.

sections.heading: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of Indian coin
sections.text: Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly performs on any Indian coin any operation which diminishes the weight or alters the composition of that coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Fraudulently or dishonestly performs an operation on Indian coin
Which diminishes its weight or alters its composition
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 246 for Indian coin.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'any of the Queen's coin'.

sections.heading: Altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description
sections.text: Whoever performs on any coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin, with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Performs an operation altering the appearance of a coin
Intending it to pass as a coin of a different description
sections.key_principle: E.g. gilding a coin to pass as a higher denomination.

sections.heading: Altering appearance of Indian coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description
sections.text: Whoever performs on any Indian coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin, with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Performs an operation altering the appearance of Indian coin
Intending it to pass as a coin of a different description
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 248 for Indian coin.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1950, for 'any of the Queen's coin'.

sections.heading: Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered
sections.text: Whoever, having coin in his possession with respect to which the offence defined in section 246 or 248 has been committed, and having known at the time when he became possessed of such coin that such offence had been committed with respect to it, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers such coin to any other person, or attempts to induce any other person to receive the same, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Possesses coin altered in the manner of s. 246 or 248, knowing so when he became possessed
Fraudulently delivers it or attempts to induce another to receive it
sections.key_principle: Uttering altered coin with guilty knowledge from the start.

sections.heading: Delivery of Indian coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered
sections.text: Whoever, having coin in his possession with respect to which the offence defined in section 247 or 249 has been committed, and having known at the time when he became possessed of such coin that such offence had been committed with respect to it, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers such coin to any other person, or attempts to induce any other person to receive the same, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Possesses Indian coin altered in the manner of s. 247 or 249, knowing so when he became possessed
Fraudulently delivers it or attempts to induce another to receive it
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 250.

sections.heading: Possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof
sections.text: Whoever fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of coin with respect to which the offence defined in either of the section 246 or 248 has been committed, having known at the time of becoming possessed thereof that such offence had been committed with respect to such coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Fraudulently in possession of coin altered under s. 246 or 248
Knew of the alteration when he became possessed of it
sections.key_principle: Guilty possession of altered coin.

sections.heading: Possession of Indian coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of coin with respect to which the offence defined in either of the section 247 or 249 has been committed having known at the time of becoming possessed thereof, that such offence had been committed with respect to such coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Fraudulently in possession of Indian coin altered under s. 247 or 249
Knew of the alteration when he became possessed of it
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 252.

sections.heading: Delivery of coin as genuine which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be altered
sections.text: Whoever delivers to any other person as genuine or as a coin of a different description from what it is, or attempts to induce any person to receive as genuine, or as a different coin from what it is, any coin in respect of which he knows that any such operation as that mentioned in sections 246, 247, 248 or 249 has been performed, but in respect of which he did not, at the time when he took it into his possession, know that such operation had been performed, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine to an amount which may extend to ten times the value of the coin for which the altered coin is passed, or attempted to be passed.
ingredients: Delivers (or attempts to induce another to receive) altered coin as genuine or as a different coin
Knows of the alteration now, but did not know when he took possession

punishment_options.condition: Up to ten times the value of the coin for which the altered coin is passed

sections.key_principle: Altered-coin counterpart of s. 241.

sections.heading: Counterfeiting Government stamp
sections.text: Whoever counterfeits, or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting, any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Counterfeits, or knowingly performs part of the process of counterfeiting
Any stamp issued by Government for revenue
sections.key_principle: Revenue stamp counterfeiting — as severe as counterfeiting Indian coin.

explanations.label: Explanation
explanations.text: A person commits this offence who counterfeits by causing a genuine stamps of one denomination to appear like a genuine stamp of a different denomination.
explanations.plain_language: Altering a genuine stamp to look like a higher denomination is counterfeiting.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by Act 26 of 1955, s. 117 and the Sch., for 'transportation for life' (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

sections.heading: Having possession of instrument or material for counterfeiting Government stamp
sections.text: Whoever has in his possession any instrument or material for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Possession of an instrument or material
For counterfeiting a Government revenue stamp, or knowing/having reason to believe so
sections.key_principle: Preparation-stage offence.

sections.heading: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Government stamp
sections.text: Whoever makes or performs any part of the process of making, or buys, or sells, or disposes of, any instrument for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Makes, buys, sells or disposes of an instrument
For counterfeiting a Government revenue stamp, or knowing/having reason to believe so
sections.key_principle: Instrument trade for stamp forgery.

sections.heading: Sale of counterfeit Government stamp
sections.text: Whoever sells, or offers for sale, any stamp which he knows or has reason to believe to be a counterfeit of any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Sells or offers for sale a stamp
Knowing or having reason to believe it is a counterfeit of a Government revenue stamp
sections.key_principle: Trading in counterfeit revenue stamps.

sections.heading: Having possession of counterfeit Government stamp
sections.text: Whoever has in his possession any stamp which he knows to be a counterfeit of any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, intending to use, or dispose of the same as a genuine stamp, or in order that it may be used as a genuine stamp, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ingredients: Possession of a stamp known to be a counterfeit of a Government revenue stamp
Intending to use or dispose of it as genuine
sections.key_principle: Possession plus intent to pass off as genuine.

sections.heading: Using as genuine a Government stamp known to be counterfeit
sections.text: Whoever uses as genuine any stamp, knowing it to be a counterfeit of any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Uses a stamp as genuine
Knowing it is a counterfeit of a Government revenue stamp
sections.key_principle: Using a counterfeit stamp (e.g. on documents).

sections.heading: Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, removes or effaces from any substance, bearing any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, any writing or document for which such stamp has been used, or removes from any writing or document a stamp which has been used for such writing or document, in order that such stamp may be used for a different writing or document, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to Government
Removes or effaces a writing/document from a stamped substance; OR removes a used stamp from a document, so that the stamp may be reused
sections.key_principle: Reuse of stamps by washing off the writing or removing a used stamp.

sections.heading: Using Government stamp known to have been before used
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, uses for any purpose a stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, which he knows to have been before used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to Government
Uses a Government revenue stamp he knows to have been used before
sections.key_principle: Using previously used stamps.

sections.heading: Erasure of mark denoting that stamp has been used
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to Government, erases or removes from a stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, any mark, put or impressed upon such stamp for the purpose of denoting that the same has been used, or knowingly has in his possession or sells or disposes of any such stamp from which such mark has been erased or removed, or sells or disposes of any such stamp which he knows to have been used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently or with intent to cause loss, erases a used-stamp mark; OR
Knowingly possesses, sells or disposes of a stamp from which the mark has been erased; OR
Sells or disposes of a stamp known to have been used
sections.key_principle: Defeating cancellation marks on revenue stamps.

sections.heading: Prohibition of fictitious stamps
sections.text: (1) Whoever— (a) makes, knowingly utters, deals in or sells any fictitious stamp, or knowingly uses for any postal purpose any fictitious stamp, or (b) has in his possession, without lawful excuse, any fictitious stamp, or (c) makes or, without lawful excuse, has in his possession any die, plate, instrument or materials for making any fictitious stamp, shall be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees. (2) Any such stamp, die, plate, instrument or materials in the possession of any person for making any fictitious stamp may be seized and, if seized shall be forfeited. (3) In this section "fictitious stamp" means any stamp falsely purporting to be issued by Government for the purpose of denoting a rate of postage, or any facsimile or imitation or representation, whether on paper or otherwise, of any stamp issued by Government for that purpose. (4) In this section and also in sections 255 to 263, both inclusive, the word "Government", when used in connection with, or in reference to any stamp issued for the purpose of denoting a rate of postage, shall, notwithstanding anything in section 17, be deemed to include the person or persons authorized by law to administer executive government in any part of India, and also in any part of Her Majesty's dominions or in any foreign country.
ingredients: (1)(a) Makes, utters, deals in, sells or uses for postal purposes any fictitious stamp; (b) possesses one without lawful excuse; (c) makes or possesses dies/plates/instruments for making one

punishment_options.condition: Of seized fictitious stamps, dies, plates, instruments and materials

sections.key_principle: Fictitious postage stamps (e.g. imitation stamps used as novelties or passed as postage) attract only a fine, with forfeiture.

subsections.text: Offences relating to fictitious (postage-like) stamps — fine up to ₹200.
Fictitious stamps and tools may be seized and, if seized, are forfeited.
'Fictitious stamp' means any stamp falsely purporting to be issued by Government to denote postage, or any facsimile/imitation/representation of one.
For ss. 255–263 'Government' in relation to postage stamps includes persons authorised to administer executive government in any part of India, Her Majesty's dominions or any foreign country.

footnotes.note_text: Added by Act 3 of 1895, s. 2.
Subs. by Act 42 of 1953, s. 4 and the Third Sch., for 'may be seized and'.

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences Relating to Weights and Measures

chapters_covered: XIII — Of Offences Relating to Weights and Measures
key_themes: Fraudulent use of false weighing instruments, weights and measures (ss. 264–265)
Possession with intent to use (s. 266)
Making or selling false weights and measures (s. 267)
notable_amendments: Act 42 of 1953 — the word 'and' omitted from s. 266.
metadata.case_query: A grocer is found with two sets of weights, one under-weight, kept under the counter; he says he never used the false set on any customer.

sections.heading: Fraudulent use of false instrument for weighing
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently uses any instrument for weighing which he knows to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently uses an instrument for weighing
Knows it to be false
sections.key_principle: Use of rigged scales; fraudulent intent and knowledge of falsity are required.

sections.heading: Fraudulent use of false weight or measure
sections.text: Whoever, fraudulently uses any false weight or false measure of length or capacity, or fraudulently uses any weight or any measure of length or capacity as a different weight or measure from what it is, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Fraudulently uses a false weight or measure of length/capacity; OR
Fraudulently uses a weight/measure as a different weight/measure from what it is
sections.key_principle: Short-weighing and mislabelled measures.

sections.heading: Being in possession of false weight or measure
sections.text: Whoever is in possession of any instrument for weighing, or of any weight, or of any measure of length or capacity, which he knows to be false, intending that the same may be fraudulently used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Possession of a false weighing instrument, weight or measure
Knows it to be false
Intending that it be fraudulently used
sections.key_principle: Possession with intent to use fraudulently.

footnotes.note_text: The word 'and' omitted by Act 42 of 1953, s. 4 and the Third Sch.

sections.heading: Making or selling false weight or measure
sections.text: Whoever makes, sells or disposes of any instrument for weighing, or any weight, or any measure of length or capacity which he knows to be false, in order that the same may be used as true, or knowing that the same is likely to be used as true, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Makes, sells or disposes of a false weighing instrument, weight or measure
Knowing it to be false
In order that it be used as true, or knowing it is likely to be so used
sections.key_principle: Manufacture and sale of false weights.

chapters.chapter_title: Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals

chapters_covered: XIV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
key_themes: Public nuisance — definition (s. 268) and punishment (ss. 290–291)
Spread of infection and quarantine (ss. 269–271)
Adulteration and sale of food and drugs (ss. 272–276)
Environmental offences — fouling water, noxious atmosphere (ss. 277–278)
Rash driving/navigation and unsafe vessels (ss. 279–283)
Negligent conduct with poison, fire, explosives, machinery, buildings, animals (ss. 284–289)
Obscenity — definition, sale, sale to young persons, public obscene acts (ss. 292–294)
Unauthorised lotteries (s. 294A)
notable_amendments: Act 8 of 1925 and Act 36 of 1969 — ss. 292–293 substituted/amended (obscenity definition and punishment).
Act 3 of 1895 — s. 294 substituted; Act 27 of 1870 — s. 294A inserted.
State amendments: Himachal Pradesh (s. 289-A, feeding monkeys), Orissa (ss. 292, 292-A, 293).
metadata.case_query: A truck driver speeding through a market lane hits and kills a pedestrian; the prosecution charges him under both s. 279 (rash driving) and s. 304A, and he argues that he can only be punished once.

sections.heading: Public nuisance
sections.text: A person is guilty of a public nuisance who does any act or is guilty of an illegal omission which causes any common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or to the people in general who dwell or occupy property in the vicinity, or which must necessarily cause injury, obstruction, danger or annoyance to persons who may have occasion to use any public right. A common nuisance is not excused on the ground that it causes some convenience or advantage.
ingredients: Any act or illegal omission
Causes common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or people in the vicinity; OR must necessarily cause injury, obstruction, danger or annoyance to persons using a public right
sections.key_principle: Public nuisance affects the community at large, not just an individual. Convenience or advantage to some does not excuse it. Punishment is residual under s. 290 (fine up to ₹200), with s. 291 for continuing after injunction. Cr.P.C. s. 133 provides summary removal.

sections.heading: Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
sections.text: Whoever unlawfully or negligently does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Unlawfully or negligently does an act
Likely to spread infection of a disease dangerous to life
Knows or has reason to believe so
sections.key_principle: Negligent spreading of dangerous infection (invoked in epidemic/pandemic contexts); knowledge or reason to believe is essential.

sections.heading: Malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
sections.text: Whoever malignantly does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Malignantly does an act
Likely to spread infection of a disease dangerous to life
Knows or has reason to believe so
sections.key_principle: Aggravated version of s. 269: 'malignantly' means with deliberate ill-will or intent to harm.

sections.heading: Disobedience to quarantine rule
sections.text: Whoever knowingly disobeys any rule made and promulgated by the Government for putting any vessel into a state of quarantine, or for regulating the intercourse of vessels in a state of quarantine with the shore or with other vessels, for regulating the intercourse between places where an infectious disease prevails and other places, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Knowingly disobeys a rule made and promulgated by Government
Rule relating to quarantine of vessels, intercourse with shore/other vessels, or intercourse between infected and other places
sections.key_principle: Quarantine breaches; knowledge of the rule is essential.

footnotes.note_text: Subs. by the A.O. 1937, for 'by the G. of I., or by any Government'.
The words 'Central or any Provincial' omitted by the A.O. 1950.
The words 'or the Crown Representative' omitted by the A.O. 1948.

sections.heading: Adulteration of food or drink intended for sale
sections.text: Whoever adulterates any article of food or drink, so as to make such article noxious as food or drink, intending to sell such article as food or drink, or knowing it to be likely that the same will be sold as food or drink, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Adulterates food or drink so as to make it noxious
Intending to sell it, or knowing it likely to be sold, as food or drink
sections.key_principle: Food adulteration making food noxious (the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 now largely governs this field).

sections.heading: Sale of noxious food or drink
sections.text: Whoever sells, or offers or exposes for sale, as food or drink, any article which has been rendered or has become noxious, or is in a state unfit for food or drink, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is noxious as food or drink, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Sells, offers or exposes for sale as food or drink an article rendered/become noxious or unfit
Knowing or having reason to believe it is noxious
sections.key_principle: Sale of noxious food; knowledge or reason to believe required.

sections.heading: Adulteration of drugs
sections.text: Whoever adulterates any drug or medical preparation in such a manner as to lessen the efficacy or change the operation of such drug or medical preparation, or to make it noxious, intending that it shall be sold or used for, or knowing it to be likely that it will be sold or used for, any medicinal purpose, as if it had not undergone such adulteration, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Adulterates a drug or medical preparation to lessen efficacy, change operation or make noxious
Intending, or knowing it likely, that it will be sold or used for medicinal purposes as if unadulterated
sections.key_principle: Drug adulteration (see also the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940).

sections.heading: Sale of adulterated drugs
sections.text: Whoever, knowing any drug or medical preparation to have been adulterated in such a manner as to lessen its efficacy, to change its operation, or to render it noxious, sells the same, or offers or exposes it for sale, or issues it from any dispensary for medicinal purposes as unadulterated, or causes it to be used for medicinal purposes by any person not knowing of the adulteration, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Knowing a drug to be adulterated (lessened efficacy, changed operation or noxious)
Sells, offers for sale, issues from a dispensary as unadulterated, or causes it to be used on an unaware person
sections.key_principle: Knowing sale or dispensing of adulterated drugs.

sections.heading: Sale of drug as a different drug or preparation
sections.text: Whoever knowingly sells, or offers or exposes for sale, or issues from a dispensary for medicinal purposes, any drug or medical preparation, as a different drug or medical preparation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Knowingly sells, offers or issues a drug/preparation
As a different drug or preparation
sections.key_principle: Substitution or mislabelling of drugs.

sections.heading: Fouling water of public spring or reservoir
sections.text: Whoever voluntarily corrupts or fouls the water of any public spring or reservoir, so as to render it less fit for the purpose for which it is ordinarily used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Voluntarily corrupts or fouls the water of a public spring or reservoir
So as to render it less fit for its ordinary use
sections.key_principle: Protects public water sources; 'voluntarily' per s. 39.

sections.heading: Making atmosphere noxious to health
sections.text: Whoever voluntarily vitiates the atmosphere in any place so as to make it noxious to the health of persons in general dwelling or carrying on business in the neighbourhood or passing along a public way, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.
ingredients: Voluntarily vitiates the atmosphere in any place
So as to make it noxious to the health of persons dwelling, doing business nearby or passing along a public way
sections.key_principle: Air pollution as a public nuisance — only a fine.

sections.heading: Rash driving or riding on a public way
sections.text: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Drives a vehicle or rides on a public way
In a rash or negligent manner
So as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person
sections.key_principle: Rash and negligent driving — no actual injury is required (danger suffices). If death results, s. 304A applies. Rashness = conscious risk-taking; negligence = want of due care.

sections.heading: Rash navigation of vessel
sections.text: Whoever navigates any vessel in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Navigates a vessel
In a rash or negligent manner
So as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury
sections.key_principle: Maritime counterpart of s. 279.

sections.heading: Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy
sections.text: Whoever exhibits any false light, mark or buoy, intending or knowing it to be likely that such exhibition will mislead any navigator, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Exhibits a false light, mark or buoy
Intending or knowing it likely to mislead a navigator
sections.key_principle: Wrecking-type offence; the high maximum reflects the danger to life at sea.

sections.heading: Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel
sections.text: Whoever knowingly or negligently conveys, or causes to be conveyed for hire, any person by water in any vessel, when that vessel is in such a state or so loaded as to endanger the life of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Knowingly or negligently conveys (or causes to be conveyed) a person by water for hire
Vessel is in such a state or so loaded as to endanger life
sections.key_principle: Unsafe boat operators (ferry/boat overloading).

sections.heading: Danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation
sections.text: Whoever, by doing any act, or by omitting to take order with any property in his possession or under his charge, causes danger, obstruction or injury to any person in any public way or public line of navigation, shall be punished, with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees.
ingredients: Does an act, or omits to take order with property in his possession/charge
Causes danger, obstruction or injury to any person in a public way or line of navigation
sections.key_principle: Obstructions and hazards on public ways — fine only.

sections.heading: Negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance
sections.text: Whoever does, with any poisonous substance, any act in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any poisonous substance in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such poisonous substance, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Does an act with a poisonous substance rashly or negligently endangering life or likely to cause hurt; OR
Knowingly or negligently omits adequate precautions with poisonous substance in his possession
sections.key_principle: Negligence with poisons; may overlap with s. 304A if death occurs.

sections.heading: Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter
sections.text: Whoever does, with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Does an act with fire/combustible matter rashly or negligently endangering life or likely to cause hurt; OR
Knowingly or negligently omits adequate precautions with fire/combustible matter in his possession
sections.key_principle: Negligent fire hazards (e.g. fireworks storage, unsafe cooking installations).

sections.heading: Negligent conduct with respect to explosive substance
sections.text: Whoever does, with any explosive substance, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any explosive substance in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from that substance, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Does an act with an explosive substance rashly or negligently endangering life; OR
Knowingly or negligently omits adequate precautions with an explosive in his possession
sections.key_principle: Negligent handling of explosives (see also the Explosives Act, 1884).

sections.heading: Negligent conduct with respect to machinery
sections.text: Whoever does, with any machinery, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any machinery in his possession or under his care as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such machinery, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Does an act with machinery rashly or negligently endangering life; OR
Knowingly or negligently omits adequate precautions with machinery in his possession or care
sections.key_principle: Industrial and machinery safety lapses.

sections.heading: Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down or repairing buildings
sections.text: Whoever, in pulling down or repairing any building, knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with that building as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from the fall of that building, or of any part thereof, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: In pulling down or repairing a building
Knowingly or negligently omits adequate precautions against probable danger to human life from its fall
sections.key_principle: Demolition and repair safety.

sections.heading: Negligent conduct with respect to animal
sections.text: Whoever knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any animal in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life, or any probable danger of grievous hurt from such animal, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ingredients: Animal in his possession
Knowingly or negligently omits adequate precautions
Against probable danger to human life or grievous hurt from the animal
sections.key_principle: Owner's liability for dangerous animals (e.g. ferocious dogs, stray bulls).

state_amendments.text: After section 289, new section 289-A: 'Feeding of Monkeys in public place.—Whoever throws eatables in public place, other than those notified by the State Government in the Official Gazette, and thereby entice monkeys to assemble at such place for taking eatables which result in causing danger to human life or to be likely to cause injury or annoyance to the public or to the people in general or to cause hindrance in smooth running of vehicular traffic, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both.'

sections.heading: Punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for
sections.text: Whoever commits a public nuisance in any case not otherwise punishable by this Code, shall be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees.
ingredients: Commits a public nuisance (s. 268)
In a case not otherwise punishable by the Code
sections.key_principle: Residual punishment for public nuisance — fine only.

sections.heading: Continuance of nuisance after injunction to discontinue
sections.text: Whoever repeats or continues a public nuisance, having been enjoined by any public servant who has lawful authority to issue such injunction not to repeat or continue such nuisance, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
ingredients: Repeats or continues a public nuisance
After a lawful injunction by a public servant not to do so
sections.key_principle: Defiance of a nuisance injunction (e.g. a Cr.P.C. s. 133 order).

sections.heading: Sale, etc., of obscene books, etc.
sections.text: (1) For the purposes of sub-section (2), a book, pamphlet, paper, writing, drawing, painting, representation, figure or any other object, shall be deemed to be obscene if it is lascivious or appeals to the prurient interest or if its effect, or (where it comprises two or more distinct items) the effect of any one of its items, is, if taken as a whole, such as to tend to deprave and corrupt persons who are likely, having regard to all relevant circumstances, to read, see or hear the matter contained or embodied in it.
